Grand Theft Auto VI is a different kind of GTA — so it needed a different kind of ending

📅 27 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (548 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: The Verge

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • GTA VI producer Rob Nelson explains Rockstar’s approach to letting players explore Vice City after the main story.
  • GTA VI producer Rob Nelson explains Rockstar’s approach to letting players explore Vice City after the main story.
  • In most Grand Theft Auto games, and most open-world games for that matter, the world is left open for you to explore once the credits roll.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

GTA VI producer Rob Nelson explains Rockstar’s approach to letting players explore Vice City after the main story.

GTA VI producer Rob Nelson explains Rockstar’s approach to letting players explore Vice City after the main story.

In most Grand Theft Auto games, and most open-world games for that matter, the world is left open for you to explore once the credits roll. It could be Los Santos or a twisted take on Manhattan, but the idea is that the main story is just one part of the experience. After that’s done, there are usually still places you haven’t explored or side missions you left lingering. But Grand Theft Auto VI doesn’t work quite the same way. Because of its storyline, which involves a couple trying to get out of the criminal life for good, that kind of ending didn’t really fit.

It has been revealed that “In this one it didn’t make sense,” Rob Nelson, producer on GTA VI and co-studio head at developer Rockstar North, told me ahead of the game’s launch. “Their story needed to end and have some kind of conclusion.”.

This story contains light spoilers for the ending of Grand Theft Auto VI, along with a key plot point from chapter 1.

To be clear, you can still play GTA VI after the main storyline wraps up. But in order for that to happen, you have to zip back in time to a moment before a pivotal decision — I won’t spoil it for you — that alters the lives of main characters Jason and Lucia, along with their young son Tomás, who they’re attempting to get custody of. Nelson says the team tried “all sorts of things” but soon realized that “in no way did it make sense” to have the game end like a traditional GTA experience.

“Their story needed to end and have some kind of conclusion.”.

According to recent reports, “You go back and have this open time again where you have the best single-player safehouse you’ve ever had in a GTA, with a garage full of supercars, a helipad, a gym, and all of the stuff you could ever want,” he notes of the solution the studio landed on. “And you can spend as long as you want there. But you don’t have Tommy. So the characters don’t have the one thing that they wanted at the start. There’s the tension where you have to spend some extra time grinding to make some more money without knowing what it’s going to get you, and it plays out differently if you get that money.”.

In a recent development, one advantage of this structure is that it lets you try out different endings. GTA VI’s story can wrap up in multiple ways based on a variety of factors: how much money you have saved up, what kind of criminal you were throughout the game, and some key decisions you’re forced to make in the final moments. The new postgame structure creates an opportunity to see some of the alternate ways the story can go. “There’s a large number of potential outcomes based on how you played it,” Nelson states.

AirTag-like trackers for Android and iPhone are everywhere nowadays, but Kodak’s latest SlideTag steps it up with a built-in E-Ink display that can show off your photos, widgets, and more along with being able to track down your items.

It has been revealed that compatible with both the Android Find Hub and Apple Find My networks, the Kodak SlideTag is a tracker inspired by the golden era of Kodak photography. The tracker is built by Reto, the same company that built the Kodak Chamera keychain digital camera.

SlideTag’s premise is relatively simple. You get a tracker with an E-Ink display and a frame in one of eight styles inspired by classic 35mm slides. Those styles are sold in a blind box format, meaning you don’t know what you’re getting until you open the box (unless you buy the full set). There’s also a ninth style that only demonstrates up in one out of every 64 boxes.

The E-Ink display can show six-color versions of your photos, or it can display things like lists, calendars, and more. There’s enough storage on the tracker for a 12-photo slideshow, synced through the Kodak Memory Link app on Android and iOS.

Connect instantly via Bluetooth to the KODAK Memory Link App. From live slideshows and custom QR codes to countdowns and dual-network tracking with Apple Find My and Google’s Find Hub, the KODAK SlideTag seamlessly integrates retro aesthetics into your everyday carry.

Kodak SlideTag is available today from Amazon.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Nvidia has announced that disgraced CEO Jensen Huang has been reinstated to the role, effective immediately.
  • It said that the board voted unanimously in favor of reinstatement despite its recent statement that it had no intention of doing so ….
  • Huang’s affair with a woman suspected to be a Chinese spy became the main headline news in the tech press after coming to light at the end of last month.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Nvidia has announced that disgraced CEO Jensen Huang has been reinstated to the role, effective immediately. The tech giant’s share price jumped more than 30% in response, with the rest of the market also making significant gains.

It said that the board voted unanimously in favor of reinstatement despite its recent statement that it had no intention of doing so ….

Huang’s affair with a woman suspected to be a Chinese spy became the main headline news in the tech press after coming to light at the end of last month. The New York Times broke the story on October 29, citing it then as “a close relationship.” Nvidia initially denied that the relationship was anything out of the ordinary.

In a recent development, that changed on November 8 when Huang publicly admitted to the affair. Nvidia’s shares dropped 5%, and the organization’s board of directors opened an independent investigation. Further details emerged over the following days. Things got even worse when the same paper reported that Huang had also had an affair with an Nvidia executive who reports to him.

That led to Huang being fired resigning on November 12.

Money over country. This is government intervention.

Despite putting the manufacturer at enormous risk and initially lying to its board of directors, there were calls in some quarters for Huang to be reinstated. He responded by saying that he would be “honored” to return if asked to do so.

The board of directors, however, said that it had no intention of inviting him back.

Nvidia’s chair Harvey Jones stated: “The board does not intend to reinstate him.”.

That changed today, with the company making the announcement in a press release.

Nvidia today declared that effective immediately, Jensen Huang has been reinstated as President and Chief Executive Officer and as a member of the Board. The Board of Directors voted unanimously to reinstate Mr. Huang following a series of discussions and meetings with Mr. Huang, after which the Board was satisfied with respect to Mr. Huang’s candor and ability to lead NVIDIA. In the process of reaching its decision, the Board received input from senior levels of the United States government, and based on that input, the Board is confident that Mr. Huang’s reinstatement poses no national security risk.

It has been revealed that “The Board believes Jensen is the right person to lead NVIDIA, and that his reinstatement is in the best interests of our stockholders, employees, partners and customers,” said Harvey C. Jones, Chair of the Board. “We have every confidence in Jensen and look forward to working with him as he resumes his leadership of the Company. We are grateful to Colette Kress for her outstanding service as interim CEO, in addition to her continuing responsibilities as NVIDIA’s Chief Financial Officer.” Harvey Jones will remain as Board chair.

Sources indicate that “I am honored to return to NVIDIA and lead one of the most consequential technology companies in the world at the beginning of a new industrial revolution,” stated Jensen Huang. “I take this responsibility with the greatest humility and renewed commitment. I want to thank the NVIDIA Board for its confidence and deliberation through this process. I am especially grateful to Harvey Jones for his leadership as Chair, and to Colette Kress and our executive staff for leading NVIDIA during this period. I am also deeply thankful to our employees, shareholders, leaders across the industry and partners around the world for their extraordinary support. Above all, I am grateful for the love and support of my family. I can’t wait to get back to work.”.

As previously declared, in light of recent reporting that Mr. Huang has been the target of a foreign intelligence effort, the Board formed a committee comprised solely of independent directors to investigate, and the committee retained independent counsel to assist it in that investigation. The Board reiterated that the committee’s investigation will proceed to conclusion. Mr. Huang fully supports the investigation and is committed to cooperating with it.

The firm’s stock price jumped by more than 30% in response, with the rest of the market also up per Yahoo Finance.

The Dow Jones Industrial Average (^DJI) jumped more than 1,200 points to recover by 2.5% following its worst week since the COVID-related sell-off in 2020. The Nasdaq Composite (^IXIC) rallied 7%.

The Sonos Arc Ultra is our favorite soundbar, and this deal brings it down to its lowest price ever. The Arc Ultra is a fantastic all-in-one solution to any home entertainment setup, with convincing, surround sound audio in a single-speaker package.

Industry observers note that if the Arc Ultra is outside your budget (or simply too dang long to fit on your media console), the compact Beam (Gen 2) is also at its lowest price ever right now. This was my home soundbar for years—it's tiny but mighty.

Want to add some serious bass in a small package? The Sonos Sub Mini is your best bet. It's smaller than most subwoofers on the market and pairs seamlessly with other Sonos speakers.

One of the only home speakers built with spatial audio in mind. The Sonos Era 300 is a great speaker, but transforms when you play Dolby Atmos tracks, activating its upfiring tweeters for more dimensionality.

This giant Sonos speaker is getting a little long in the tooth (it rolled out in 2020), but it still delivers the strongest, most bass-heavy sound of any single Sonos speaker.

In a recent development, sonos' smallest speaker, the Roam 2, is a handheld portable Bluetooth speaker you can basically take anywhere. What separates it from the pack (and Sonos' Bluetooth speakers generally) is that they also connect to Wi-Fi to sync up with your home speakers.

A step up from the Roam 2, the Sonos Play is one of the brand's newest portable speakers, and one of its best, according to former WIRED reviewer Ryan Waniata.

I would argue that the Sonos Move 2 is more of a portable home Bluetooth speaker than a lightweight, compact, throw-it-in-your-bag for a trip to the beach-type speaker like the Roam 2 and Play above. Think of it like a portable, dust and water resistant version of the Era 100.

The new Sonos Ace Ultra headphones are not on sale, but the capable originals are. The Sonos Ace don't connect or sync to other Sonos products like the brand's speakers do, but they are capable stand-alone headphones, with clear sound, a comfortable fit, and a surprisingly good transparency mode.

This gaming mouse should be a Logitech-killer, but it has one massive flaw

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Keychron’s G6 HE uses magnetic switches like Logitech’s Superstrike mice, but the clicks are all off.﻿.
  • Keychron’s G6 HE uses magnetic switches like Logitech’s Superstrike mice, but the clicks are all off.﻿.
  • In a recent development, if you buy something from a link, The Verge may earn a commission.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Keychron’s G6 HE uses magnetic switches like Logitech’s Superstrike mice, but the clicks are all off.﻿.

Keychron’s G6 HE uses magnetic switches like Logitech’s Superstrike mice, but the clicks are all off.﻿.

In a recent development, if you buy something from a link, The Verge may earn a commission. See our ethics statement.

It has been revealed that when Keychron confirmed its $90 G6 HE gaming mouse, I immediately thought, “Cool! A cheaper alternative to the pricey $180 Logitech G Pro X2 Superstrike.” Logitech’s innovation with the Superstrike is using magnetic Hall effect switches for a user-adjustable mouse click depth, with haptic vibrations mimicking the tactile click feel. The Keychron G6 HE, as its name indicates, also uses Hall effect switches for that same kind of customization. But something felt immediately off as I began testing it.

The mouse’s shape and design are very reminiscent of Logitech G Pro models, with more colorful flair. The magnetic switches are there and easily customizable (through a browser-based app, no less). But the clicks? The clicks are all wrong.

The left and right mouse buttons on the G6 HE use Keychron’s MagOptic switches, which are both magnetic Hall effect and optical. They click just like any standard mouse, regardless of where you set the actuation point. There are no fancy haptics on the Keychron. If you set the buttons to a shallow hair-trigger depth, you’ll register a press before you actually feel or hear any click. Set the depth for a very heavy press, and the mouse clicks before it actually registers. That… kind of defeats the purpose here.

In a recent development, there’s not much point in tuning the actuation depth of the G6 HE’s buttons if the click feel doesn’t match it. I suppose it’s still nice to have a hair-trigger-like setting for taking faster single shots in an FPS, but not feeling anything when you shoot is weird. And it gets frustrating when using the G6 HE as a regular mouse for productivity — like you’re getting phantom clicks as you mouse around your computer. At least I can feel my accidental clicks when using a Logitech Superstrike with the action set too high, and I know I’m to blame for leaving the mouse on my try-hard settings.

I reached out to Keychron for the reasoning behind the G6 HE’s magnetic-but-not-haptic setup, and cofounder Fab Chan said, “There are two reasons for this design. First, many people still prefer the feel of a traditional click over haptics. Second, a haptic motor adds weight, and for this model we prioritized a lighter design. That said, we’re planning a model with haptic feedback. It will be slightly heavier than the G6 HE, and we’ll share more details soon.”.

The G6 HE is a lightweight mouse. It’s only 49g with its battery, or 40g in wired mode with the battery removed. The Logitech X2 Superstrike is 60g, and the newer X3 Superstrike is 59g — each still pretty light. If you ignore all the Hall effect stuff and just use the G6 HE as a regular mouse, it has some things going for it over the Superstrikes. In addition to its lighter build and much lower price, it feels a tiny bit comfier in my hand, thanks to its side walls that curve slightly inward at the bottom.

One of its best features is hot-swappable batteries. From my time testing Angry Miao’s AM Infinity Mouse, I know that once you can pop out a magnetic battery pack and rapidly swap it, you never want to go back to plugging in your mouse to charge. You can also get the G6 HE in black with a standard built-in rechargeable battery for $15 less, but I don’t think that’s enough savings to forgo the convenience of hot-swap batteries.

The G6 HE’s charging base doubles as the wireless receiver, and of course it’s lit up with customizable RGB lighting. It has four programmable buttons for on-the-fly changes to things like DPI, lighting, mouse profiles, or just about anything else you want to program. The browser-based Keychron Launcher software is robust and makes tinkering with the G6 HE or its base very easy. And for some reason, the receiver / charging base is designed like a vacuum tube, which is fun, but it means you’re unscrewing its clear housing to access the battery — a little tedious.

In a recent development, I can’t shake my disappointment with the G6 HE’s lackadaisical magnetic switch implementation. Keychron seems proud of the fancy MagOptic Switch it put into the G6 HE, even going so far as to call it “next gen,” but this mouse seems a jack of all trades and master of none. The G6 HE is cheaper than most other mice with hot-swap batteries — which can still make it worthwhile if you don’t care about all the Hall effect stuff — but that is its lone saving grace.

We’ll have to wait and see if Keychron’s follow-up model with haptics can properly compete with the Superstrike mice and their hallmark feature. I’m excited to see where Hall effect tech goes in mice, and how more companies can evolve it, but the G6 HE is a half-measure.

The OnePlus website in India is unaffected and still selling devices.

The warranty website OnePlus links to appears to be more than a bit out of date, with a focus on 2023’s OnePlus Open. The most recent device mentioned is the OnePlus 13, though the page has been updated based on what we’re able to see on the Wayback Machine.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Managing a YouTube watchlist shouldn’t be as frustrating as it is, especially on the most-used app in my life. Google’s premier streaming app has too many issues with resurfacing content; in my opinion, this is now a major problem that needs to be fixed.

Aside from my YouTube watchlist gripes, it’s no secret that moving from a web browser to the TV is ultimately still a frustrating experience.

In a recent development, lots of things I love about watching videos on my laptop or PC just don’t translate well to when I’m sat on my sofa holding a remote trying to find something to watch after wrapping up for the day. One thing I’m getting annoyed with is how YouTube scales on TV and Android TV boxes because you’re given less choice and arguably poorer recommendations for content due to the constraints in place.

According to recent reports, understandably, you can’t compress the layout too much on a TV as you’re typically sat a few feet away and all aspects of the interface need to be legible. I would still like to tweak it, though, if that were possible.

It has been revealed that maybe we could get proper sections for content, like how Netflix and other streaming platforms offer categorized areas where you can search for “comedy” or “horror”. I’m almost certain that, with Google’s insane investment and massive AI push, where every video is already analyzed hundreds of times, that wouldn’t be too difficult to do.

It has been revealed that the problem now is that the sidebar menu is just too broad. Gaming covers basically everything. Then each line of videos accounts for one title, but requires search and previous watch data to populate. I find myself often fighting with recommendations on my TV, whereas on desktop it’s not as much of a problem.

That leads me to my biggest problem with YouTube, and it’s the, frankly, embarrassing watchlist or “Watch later” controls.

It has been revealed that I can’t fault that it works, but right now the watchlist function is like something out of the early 2000s due to the lack of flexibility that I touched on above. As my YouTube consumption has increased 20x over the past four or five years, managing what I want to come back to or might have missed the first time around is starting to become a bit of a chore.

I’ve tried using playlists to save things, but things get messy very promptly because of how cumbersome it is to a) create a playlist on TV and b) how playlists are organized by default.

Google TV isn’t perfect, but it’s where I keep my biggest TV and movie watchlist outside of YouTube. Yes, YouTube is mostly for user-generated content, but I would take something as basic as Google TV’s interface baked into YouTube somehow. Add in categorization and auto-clear.

Industry observers note that the Watch Later section has become an unwieldy place that I never really want to go unless I desperately have to. I’m constantly losing videos that I hoped to come back to or have an affinity for.

It has been revealed that videos don’t clear automatically, nor do you know when they were added. Yes, I’ll give credit that you can sort by a few options, but that’s the bare minimum. The process of moving things around is slow and takes multiple taps. Watch Later is also hidden compared to other services. It’s under your account, then beneath “Liked videos,” which is below any you may have uploaded yourself.

Industry observers note that on a TV, the process is so annoying I just avoid it altogether. You go to the sidebar menu > Library > Watch later. It should be front-and-center on a TV. It’s almost unforgivable in my eyes because even your watch history is given greater prominence. I simply cannot understand that decision.

Recent findings suggest that I’m not always a huge fan of AI being shoehorned into apps and services, but this is one of those areas that has been left to rot for a while and could get a massive uplift from adding in a little bit of Gemini. Even if it were just an enhanced search function or more tools for organizing.

With YouTube TV effectively taking over regular broadcast television and being the world’s biggest streaming platform, I’m shocked by how so many areas of the platform remain in a consistently neglected state.

It has been revealed that A little bit of spit and polish, and maybe I’ll start using this section again. For now, though, I’ll stick to texting myself links of stuff I want to watch. The ball is in your court, Google.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

You can have a good time brewing up widgets — as long as you don’t expect too much.﻿.

You can have a good time brewing up widgets — as long as you don’t expect too much.﻿.

Aside from dealing with my calendar, there’s one thing I want AI to do: tell me if I’m about to miss the bus.

It has been revealed that what I need is a widget. It needs to tell me real-time arrivals for the bus stop near my house. Tapping around on my phone screen to open the right app and select my stop will slow me down enough to miss a bus. I need glanceable information, and I hoped that Android’s vibe-coded widget feature could help me out here. It hasn’t, to my disappointment, but I still had a good time cooking up other widgets.

Industry observers note that google declared the ability to create custom widgets using AI back at I/O in the spring. It’s called Create My Widget, and it’s part of Android’s suite of “Gemini Intelligence” features. It’s in beta, and only just started rolling out to Pixel phones earlier this month. I was hyped. Not only does this feature raise tantalizing questions like “What is an app?” and “Where does the app live?” — stuff we live for here at The Verge dot com — it has potential to help me make my home screen ridiculous.

Sources indicate that I fired it up on a Pixel 11 Pro and cooked up my first few widgets, including one that demonstrates a different quote from Jurassic Park every hour — the original film, not any of the sequels, naturally. It took about 20 seconds to make, and it rules. Tapping the widget opens a thread in r/MovieQuotes, so there’s not much software magic going on under the hood, evidently. But did it bring me real joy to read the words “That is one substantial pile of shit,” on my home screen? It did.

In a recent development, I also made a widget that will display the words “Tut tut, looks like rain” whenever it’s raining. This is silly, and it accomplishes nothing except making me happy. I couldn’t think of anything clever it should say when there’s no rain, so it just notes “No rain right now” otherwise. But I live in Seattle, so I’ll get a lot of mileage out of this widget.

The create-a-widget interface suggests a few ideas and categories, leaning on more practical uses like habit trackers and recipe inspiration. Fine, I’ll try something normal, I thought. I’m trying to get better about my daily mental health walk, so I had it make a widget for logging a week’s worth of walks. I was hoping for something visual that would trick my little monkey brain into keeping a streak going. Instead, I got something simply labeled “Log Walk” that triggers Gemini to add a walk to my calendar when I tap it. At least Gemini suggested the extra step of creating a checklist where I could mark off the days of the week as I completed my little walk.

In a recent development, it took me a minute to get my head around it, but many of the widgets are basically little prompt shortcuts for Gemini. You tap one, it pulls up the Gemini interface on your home screen, thinks for a while, then comes up with whatever you were asking for. The kinds of widgets you can make also seem to fit into some well-defined templates. You can create a widget that displays a countdown to a holiday or certain event on your calendar. You can show a recent score and upcoming game time for your favorite sports team. For anything more open ended, your widget will pull from Google search results (suggest a different three-ingredient cocktail recipe every day, for example) or prompt Gemini to figure it out for you. I was hoping for mini apps I could customize to my liking, but this is more of a one-size-fits-all feature. Fair, I guess.

I was hoping for mini apps I could customize to my liking, but this is more of a one-size-fits-all feature.

Sources indicate that that’s why my bus schedule widget didn’t really work out. I asked for a list of real-time arrivals; it gave me a tile that reads “Bus Arrivals” and uses Gemini to search for arrival times for the stop I specified. Gemini is helpful for some things but useless for this; it gives me a wordy response about how often the bus runs and when I might expect it to arrive based on the schedule. Not what I had in mind. On the bright side, my Jurassic Park quote widget had some words of wisdom for me: “Life, uh, finds a way.” That’ll do for now.

Will Siri AI threaten Apple’s environmental target, given Google and Meta admissions?

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1007 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: 9to5mac

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that I think Apple can reasonably claim to be the leading tech giant when it comes to its environmental credentials.
  • All of this could potentially be put at risk by the company’s ambitions for Siri AI, however, as Meta joins Google in admitting it is now unlikely to meet its own 2030 net zero promise, thanks to the huge power demands of the data centers powering its AI services ….
  • In a recent development, apple’s environmental record isn’t entirely perfect.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that I think Apple can reasonably claim to be the leading tech giant when it comes to its environmental credentials. It has led the way with its use of renewable energy, made significant strides with carbon-neutral production, and removed plastic from all its packaging.

All of this could potentially be put at risk by the company’s ambitions for Siri AI, however, as Meta joins Google in admitting it is now unlikely to meet its own 2030 net zero promise, thanks to the huge power demands of the data centers powering its AI services ….

In a recent development, apple’s environmental record isn’t entirely perfect. For example, when it claimed that the Apple Watch Series 9 and Ultra 2 were carbon neutral back in 2023, that claim was described as “bogus,” with the EU banning Apple from repeating it. The company has also been criticized for pushing a relentless annual iPhone cycle, encouraging frequent upgrades.

In a recent development, overall, however, Apple has first-rate credentials when it comes to the environment. It was way back in 2018 when the manufacturer hit its goal of running its own operations off 100% renewable energy. This includes all Apple facilities, from Apple Park through data centers to its worldwide retail store network.

I said at the time that using more environmentally friendly packaging should be the organization’s next priority, and it has indeed made great progress with this over the years, succeeding in removing all plastic packaging earlier this year.

In a recent development, after its own operations, Apple set about trying to tackle the power usage of its manufacturing partners. Back in 2020, the company set a goal of having its entire supply chain be carbon neutral by 2030. Just four years later, Apple remarked it was 95% of the way there.

Recent findings suggest that the company also helps fund and support a wide range of environmental initiatives around the world. Just a few examples include conservation in China’s national parks, environmental protection and carbon removal in Australia and Fresh Zealand, and helping to fund the build-out of renewable energy capacity in India.

Recent findings suggest that potentially, however, the vast energy demands of the data centers powering AI services could put its 2030 goal at risk. Other tech giants have already admitted that it may lead them to fail to hit their own renewable energy promises.

In a recent development, back in 2024, for example, Google CEO Sundar Pichai remarked that the AI boom was “challenging” to the company’s 2030 carbon-free goal. CNET reports that Meta is now also admitting that it may fail to hit the same target.

Meta’s data center and sustainability chiefs wrote that the firm is “re-evaluating our timelines, sequencing, and interim milestones — including the 2030 timeframe for our net zero emissions goal and our near-term intensity targets.” In an emailed statement to CNET, a Meta spokesperson added, “We remain committed to net zero, but are re-evaluating the 2030 timeline.”.

Notably, a lot of Siri’s most advanced AI capabilities are currently powered by Google’s Gemini models.

Recent findings suggest that at the same 2024 event where Google expressed doubts, Apple reiterated its commitment to its 2030 target. Then-CEO Tim Cook repeated this assurance later the same year, although admitted it would be challenging.

It has been revealed that more challenges, yes. But are we coming off the goal? No, definitely not. With more data centers, you use more renewable energy, and we’ve built that muscle now […] I feel very good about 2030.

In the company’s most recent environmental progress report, it said that it was was still using 100% renewable energy despite using over 2.5 billion kWh of electricity to power its data centers.

Sources indicate that we’re proud that 100 percent of that electricity came from renewable sources including solar, wind, and low-impact hydropower. To cover our needs, we build our own renewable power projects and work with utilities to purchase clean energy from locally obtained resources. We’re staying at 100 percent even as Apple’s data center capacity continues to grow.

The same report said the company had achieved zero water use for cooling at its latest data centers.

At our three newest data centers, we use high-efficiency air-cooled chillers instead of water-cooled systems, resulting in zero water use for cooling.

However, the greatest challenge for Apple lies ahead. The reason that Google and Meta are now backtracking on their promises is that both companies now have massive AI capabilities. As yet, Apple does not.

What happens as Apple expands Siri AI capabilities as usage increases, and as the tech giant moves into agentic AI features? Is it realistic for the company to maintain its 100% track record with vastly greater data center energy usage?

Greenpeace expressed its own doubts earlier this year.

“AI will be the defining test of Apple’s climate commitments,” spokesperson Avex Li indicates. “To preserve Tim Cook’s environmental legacy, the company will need to show that AI growth can be accommodated within its existing climate commitments through absolute emissions reductions, additional renewable energy investment, and longer-lasting products.”.

Apple did not respond directly but merely pointed to its past statements and most recent environmental progress report.

I don’t doubt the company’s desire to maintain its track record, but if Apple does join the likes of Google and Meta in becoming a major AI player, sticking to its 2030 timing is going to become increasingly difficult.

Do you think Apple will succeed? Please share your thoughts in the comments.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, spaceX shares rose in premarket trading amid a broader tech rally and after CEO Elon Musk expanded his SpaceX share-donation initiative for U.S. children.

Substantial Tech stocks, including Nvidia, Intel, Marvell, AMD and Micron were all higher in premarket trading as the sector rebounded from a heavy selloff earlier this week.

SpaceX had jumped more than 7% in overnight trading on Blue Ocean ATS after Musk posted about donating shares on X.

"I will be donating another share of SpaceX to all kids in America every year," Musk mentioned in the post.

Blue Ocean ATS is an alternative trading system for U.S. equities that operates from 8 p.m. to 4 a.m. ET, outside regular U.S. stock market hours. According to the platform's holiday schedule, overnight trading resumed at 8 p.m. ET on Thanksgiving Day. U.S. stock exchanges were closed Thursday and are scheduled to close early Friday.

SpaceX stock was last 4% higher in premarket trading. Shares closed 1.30% higher on Wednesday ahead of Thanksgiving.

The latest pledge follows SpaceX's announcement Wednesday that it would donate one share of its Class A stock to every active Trump Account, tax-advantaged investment account for American children, with Musk personally matching the gift.

In a separate post on X, Musk mentioned SpaceX's contribution would be transferred next month, while his personal donation would follow when his lockup period expires in June next year.

Nearly 70 million Trump Accounts had been created as of October, according to the White House.

Since the program's launch in July, families and friends have contributed more than $1 billion to the accounts, bringing total deposits from all sources to more than $9 billion, CNBC reported earlier this week.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Garmin and Bark are competing for your money this year, and these sales make it easy to get something fun that’ll keep your kids safe and in touch.

In a recent development, if you’re anything like me, you didn’t give your kids a phone or tablet the second they were out of the womb. Instead, I’ve slowly introduced them to personal devices as I felt it made sense, and a smartwatch was one of the first easy ways for them to stay in touch while away from home without being introduced to the dangers of the internet. This year’s Black Friday sales on Bark and Garmin kids’ smartwatches slash up to $64 off the regular price, making them an easier decision than ever to pick up.

I’ve tested a lot of kids’ smartwatches over the years, and I can easily recommend the two in the picture above: the Bark Watch and the Garmin Bounce 2. Choosing between the two is easy enough. Garmin’s watch is simpler and comes in a slightly more durable case with fun colors. It’s slightly cheaper than Bark, but doesn’t have any health sensors on board. It mainly tracks steps, allows your kids to message or call you, and gives you geofencing and location tracking through a $9.99 per month LTE subscription plan. It’s got a 5ATM rating and a polycarbonate case, so it’s quite durable.

Industry observers note that the Garmin Bounce 2 is preloaded with a few mini games and educational apps, plus the Garmin Jr. app has built-in unlockables and rewards parents can set for doing chores, completing schoolwork, etc. Battery life is roughly 2 days with normal use, but can be less if you’re in an area with poor LTE reception. The Garmin Bounce 2 is best for kids 10 and under.

Industry observers note that the Bark Watch uses Samsung Galaxy Watch 8 hardware and a custom version of Wear OS. It’s a much more powerful watch and only gets a day of battery life because of it. This one feels like a midpoint between a kids’ watch and a standard Wear OS watch, as it has all the power of Wear OS but doesn’t feature the Google Play Store. It doesn’t have any games, social media, or browsers.

Sources indicate that since it uses Samsung’s hardware, it includes cutting-edge health sensors that your kids can use, plus great multitasking and a svelte, attractive design. Bark charges $15 per month for its plan, which includes a Bark App subscription for the whole family. I also use the Bark App on my son’s phone, which helps me monitor his usage and make sure he’s safe online. The extra $5 per month adds up, but it’s absolutely worth it if you want to add the Bark App to another phone or tablet.

The Bark Watch is fine enough for younger kids, but the design and lack of games feel more like an “older kids’ watch” to me, and my 12-year-old son agrees. Either way you go, these are fantastic choices that you’ll be happy with, especially with a nice little deal.

In a recent development, I have to be honest here: most streaming deals aren't going to turn your finances around in any life-changing way. The Black Friday streaming price cuts have become steadily less tempting over the past few years. They're just not as impressive as they used to be. It's also worth noting that most deals apply only to the ad-supported tiers (with just a few exceptions). Still, any and every discount is welcome in a time when prices keep rising. Every cent counts, and it's easy to lose track of just how much you spend on streaming — especially if you're signed up for more than one service.

According to recent reports, most streamers declared their Black Friday deals early this week, but you may be wondering if there are still more to come. With just a few days until Cyber Monday, I'd say the best streaming deals have already arrived. I can't imagine that many more will pop up at this stage.

I'm shocked that Peacock's Black Friday deal is as good as it is for 2026. Last year, the streamer didn't offer a deal at all, so this is light-years better than I was expecting. If you've been holding off on subscribing, now is likely the only time you'll get a decent discount. The Paramount+, HBO Max, and Disney+/Hulu Black Friday offers are pretty much on par with their deals of years past. I would lock in HBO Max and the Disney+/Hulu bundle for a full year, as more price increases could pop up in 2027. Paramount+ tends to offer discounts throughout the year more than any other streamer, so if you miss out on this one, it's no biggie.

It's not worth holding on for a Netflix Black Friday deal, unfortunately. Netflix has never offered a Black Friday discount, or any kind of discount for that matter. Netflix is the top name in streaming and obviously feels that it doesn't need to offer Black Friday deals. I don't expect this year to be any different, but I'm always willing to be proven wrong. It would be a nice and welcome surprise.

We'll be updating this list of the best Black Friday streaming deals on the off chance any more turn up, so be sure to check back for updates.

German software firm SAP is reportedly cutting at least 10,000 jobs in AI push

📅 27 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (484 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: CNBC

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • SAP is preparing a strategy to eliminate at least 10,000 positions as the German firm reshapes its software business for the artificial intelligence era, Bloomberg reported on Thursday, citing people familiar with the matter.
  • "The business environment in which we operate is changing rapidly through AI, and we are continuously reviewing how our organization and workforce need to evolve to remain successful," SAP noted in a statement to CNBC.
  • Recent findings suggest that "As part of this ongoing transformation, roles and functions will naturally change over time.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

SAP is preparing a strategy to eliminate at least 10,000 positions as the German firm reshapes its software business for the artificial intelligence era, Bloomberg reported on Thursday, citing people familiar with the matter.

"The business environment in which we operate is changing rapidly through AI, and we are continuously reviewing how our organization and workforce need to evolve to remain successful," SAP noted in a statement to CNBC.

Recent findings suggest that "As part of this ongoing transformation, roles and functions will naturally change over time. Beyond this, no decisions have been made regarding any further measures. We do not comment on speculation.".

The tech giant did not provide any further details on potential job cuts.

The report came as the manufacturer flagged a cybersecurity attack, but remarked it had found "no evidence of unauthorized access to customer business data.".

"SAP has identified suspicious activity and promptly implemented the necessary measures to protect its customers and preserve the security of its services," a tech giant spokesperson noted.

"Our customers trust us to protect their data, and that remains our highest priority. In a highly dynamic threat environment, we will continue to strengthen our security to provide the secure and resilient environment our customers depend on.".

It has been revealed that other software companies have also tied workforce reductions to AI initiatives, though for different reasons. WiseTech Global said in February it planned to cut about 2,000 jobs over two years as it integrated AI into its products and operations.

Atlassian noted in March it would cut about 1,600 jobs partly to fund further AI investment, while Cloudflare said in May it would eliminate more than 1,100 roles as it moved toward an AI-first operating model.

According to recent reports, in the U.S., employers cited AI in 121,401 job-cut announcements through October 2026, accounting for about 20% of the total, according to a Nov. 5 report from outplacement and executive coaching firm Challenger, Gray & Christmas.

SAP employs more than 110,000 people worldwide. Bloomberg reported that all departments had been asked to identify potential cuts, with product, engineering and sales in particular focus.

The company also underwent a reorganization in 2024, when it eliminated around 10,000 positions through a program that relied mainly on voluntary departures and retraining.

Its headcount later remained relatively flat as it hired for latest roles, Bloomberg reported.

In 2023, SAP CEO Christian Klein told CNBC he did not necessarily expect a reduction in the workforce, saying he expected the firm to grow and "accelerate" its total revenue.

The reported cuts come as Klein pushes SAP toward an AI-first strategy. This year, SAP completed four acquisitions — Reltio, Dremio, Prior Labs and TechWolf — and made strategic investments in AI-focused companies including Parloa, n8n and Conduct.

The acquisitions are intended to help SAP organize firm data, develop AI models for business information and analyze workforce skills.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Xreal offers an impressively wide range of smart display glasses that give you a massive virtual display without the massive price tag.

Xreal makes my favorite pairs of smart display glasses, and all of the tech giant’s standalone pairs are on sale for the big weekend. Xreal glasses plug into any device that supports USB-C display out (your phone, handheld gaming system, laptop, etc.) and deliver a giant virtual screen only visible inside the glasses, giving you a personal home theater to enjoy your content on. Here’s the Black Friday sale in ascending price order:.

Personally, I would recommend the least expensive of the bunch, the Xreal xbx a01+. It’s on sale for $249 ($50 off) and sports the most stylish looks of the three options, plus the lightest weight at 62g, the brightest display at 1600 nits, and class-leading 3,840Hz PWM dimming. It’s even got smooth tracking that’ll keep you from feeling sick when using them in a moving vehicle. I find these the most comfortable, by far, and have taken them with me on every flight since they released a few months ago in the summer.

According to recent reports, choosing between the Xreal 1S and Xreal One Pro is a little harder, so let’s cover the pricing and differences that you’ll care most about. Xreal 1S is on sale for $379 ($70 off) and offers true native 3DoF spatial tracking, built-in real-time 3D conversion of 2D content, and a fully adjustable screen size and distance. Those are all upgrades over the xbx a01+ model.

Xreal One Pro is on sale for $499 ($100 off) and upgrades the Xreal 1S experience with prism lenses and a wider field of view. There are no other functional differences between One Pro and 1S other than the wider field of view and flatter lenses, so if those aren’t a substantial deal to you, the Xreal 1S is the “Goldilocks” pick because of its price and the range of features it offers.

Xreal 1 Pro+, on sale for the first time, upgrades the experience even further, offering a peak 1,200-nit brightness, a new AI HDR option, upgrading the 2D-to-3D conversion to 60FPS, adding extra viewing modes, and swapping out the nose pad for a more comfortable design.

In a recent development, lastly, is Xreal Asus ROG R1 glasses, which are also on sale for the first time. You can choose between the normal style or the 20th anniversary style for the same $749 price. This one comes with a 240Hz display, an entire dock that connects to your PC or console of choice, more settings than any other Xreal glasses to date (making it feel like a proper monitor replacement), and that trademark Asus ROG style.

In a recent development, if you haven’t used a pair of smart display glasses from Xreal before, the setup is simple. Just plug the USB-C cable into your phone, laptop, or gaming handheld, and you’ll be greeted with a giant virtual screen that floats in front of your face. It’s like having a huge TV on the go, and it always looks great thanks to the micro-OLED image quality and tinted lenses. Only Xreal Aura differs from this setup, as it’s a completely standalone, VR headset-like experience in a significantly smaller form factor.

Industry observers note that if you buy something from a link, The Verge may earn a commission. See our ethics statement.

Laptop prices have been a hot-button topic all year long thanks to RAMageddon. We’ve seen existing models get more expensive and fresh models arrive at higher prices than last-gen — sometimes with lower specs, too. 2026 in general has been a bad time to buy a computer. But thankfully, Black Friday can offer a tiny bit of respite.

Recent findings suggest that if the computer you right now use is working well for you, good. Happy for you. But if you’re in the market for something more powerful, bigger, smaller, thinner, etc. — and you prefer new over used — you can currently save some decent dough on MacBooks, Windows notebooks, and gaming laptops.

The big, multi-hundred-dollar savings are typically reserved for higher-end models with bigger specs, like Windows models running Nvidia’s newly introduced Arm-based RTX Spark platform — which are getting their first major discounts. More budget-friendly laptops are also receiving decent discounts right now, though, including the MacBook Neo. The current $100 discount on Apple’s budget laptop might seem like small potatoes considering it’s just a return to its original price, but it’s the best you can do for now (if you can’t hold out for a rumored new one in 2027).

Recent findings suggest that as always, the deals below are for laptops we’ve reviewed or tested firsthand in some way at The Verge — either that exact model or a similar one we expect to be equally good. There are many laptops out there and myriad deals running now through Cyber Monday, but if any of these fit your needs, you can’t go wrong.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

iOS 27.3 launches soon with a key change: certain advanced AI features will have daily usage limits. In an article posted on X, leaker pdfu details how this latest system works.

When iOS 27.3, macOS 27.3, and iPadOS 27.3 arrive next month, Apple will implement usage limits for advanced AI features.

It has been revealed that some Apple Intelligence capabilities will continue having unlimited use—mainly ones that run locally. But for server-based features that use Private Cloud Compute (PCC), users will have daily allowances on a per-device basis.

Apple has shared some official word on how usage limits work, but many of the finer details haven’t been publicized yet. However, leaker pdfu has discovered a lot about the behind-the-scenes rules governing usage limits. Many were shared this week in an article posted on X.

For example, here’s each feature’s “standard device limit” in daily tokens per pdfu:.

According to recent reports, as explained in pdfu’s article, token usage depends on the complexity of requests. He writes:.

Not all features make the same number of requests. Generating one image in Image Playground, or a single query to the AFM 3 Cloud model in Shortcuts, consumes one token. Siri AI requests may make multiple connections to PCC, as server models make tool calls and receive results. Here’s a timeline of how the query “Find a bookshop near me that’s open right now” uses 2 Siri tokens:.

In a recent development, it’s also worth noting that not all Siri AI requests will use tokens—only “advanced” requests. If you’re interested in reading more, pdfu also recently outlined what counts as an “advanced” Siri request, which you can read here.

Industry observers note that do you expect these usage limits in iOS 27.3 to be a problem for you? Let us know in the comments.

Chinese chip stocks notch biggest ever one-day gains as Beijing signals broader market support

📅 27 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (732 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNBC

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Chinese stocks rebounded sharply on Friday after a rare intraday state media readout cheered investors as top policymakers pledged to expand the role of state-backed funds in supporting the market.
  • The STAR index surged 14%, led by Chinese chipmakers such as CXMT, Cambricon and SMIC.
  • Recent findings suggest that the gains were widespread across mainland and Hong Kong stock indexes.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Chinese stocks rebounded sharply on Friday after a rare intraday state media readout cheered investors as top policymakers pledged to expand the role of state-backed funds in supporting the market.

The STAR index surged 14%, led by Chinese chipmakers such as CXMT, Cambricon and SMIC. The CSI Semiconductor index of 40 chip stocks climbed by 17.6% in its biggest single-day gain on record, surpassing the prior record of nearly 17% in late 2024, according to Wind Information.

Recent findings suggest that the gains were widespread across mainland and Hong Kong stock indexes. The Hang Seng index rose 2%, while the CSI 300 index climbed 4%, its biggest jump since October 2024, according to Wind data.

The rally comes as governments pour support into domestic chip industries while tightening controls on sensitive technology in the global race for artificial intelligence.

The U.S. unveiled a newly introduced rule last week to further restrict Chinese companies’ access to advanced AI chips, including through overseas data centers, adding pressure on Beijing to accelerate its push for semiconductor self-sufficiency.

Friday's rally comes after the CSI 300 on Thursday sank to its lowest level since the escalation of the U.S.-China tariff war in the spring of 2025, according to Wind data.

Industry observers note that in recent months, investors have weighed the commercial feasibility of Chinese artificial intelligence developers and tighter U.S. restrictions on advanced chips.

Chinese Premier Li Qiang oversaw a meeting Friday morning of the State Council, the country's top governing body, which saw officials pledge to strengthen the role of "National Team" — referring to state-backed funds — to stabilize markets and ensure ample liquidity, according to a readout released by state media Xinhua News.

The explicit reference to the "national team" is a first for a State Council meeting, said Bob Chen, a Shanghai-based venture capitalist and economist.

Authorities also stressed that "capital markets are crucial to the broader economy," according to the readout, a rare comment from a government that has not always looked favorably on the financial sector.

"Stock market performance is now prioritized at the highest level for the Chinese government," which is boosting investor confidence, Chen remarked.

"That's very strong language from the top officials," noted Zong Ke, a portfolio manager at a Shanghai-based quantitative fund.

Recent findings suggest that by Ke's calculations, stock trading volumes surged rapidly after the readout was released around 1:00 p.m. local time (12:00 a.m. ET). Full-day turnover across the Shanghai, Shenzhen and Beijing exchanges was 52% higher than the previous session.

Policymakers also vowed to strengthen the role of "stabilization funds" like Central Huijin Investment, a state-owned investment firm that holds equity stakes on behalf of the State Council.

Sources indicate that that message "effectively institutionalized Central Huijin's role as a state stabilization fund," mentioned Hong Hao, managing partner of Lotus Asset Management. "And it's significantly positive news for the market.".

Hao expects this market rally to prove more durable than the "fleeting bounce" triggered by Beijing's stimulus talks in the past, which wore off in days. "This time it's for real.".

The readout of the Cabinet's meeting, typically released well after trading hours, was published around noon local time during trading hours, an unusual timing that's viewed by markets as a bullish signal.

The State Council also pledged better policies to steer medium- or long-term funds, such as insurance and social security funds, into equities, and encouraged listed companies to pay more dividends and step up share buybacks, while vowing a crackdown on financial fraud to protect investors.

The national team will accelerate asset purchases, Ke stated, adding that he expects more supportive policies to follow, such as further loosening the institutional constraints that have limited long-term funds from investing in stocks.

Beijing's reliance on intervention to offset stock volatility has, however, raised questions about the market's ability to sustain longer-term gains.

But the market needs this kind of support right now, noted Ke, as the near-term aim is to ease liquidity pressure and restore confidence so the market doesn't fall much further.

Chinese AI-related stocks also carry less downside risk than their U.S. counterparts, as the companies have spent less on AI so far and their shares have already been through a sharp correction, Ke said.

That, together with the pledged state backing, has given investors more confidence that the market may be nearing its bottom, Ke added.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

We can blame AI for many things, least of all the steep increase in the cost of integral storage and memory we need for PCs, Macs, phones, and consoles.

I don’t know if you’re aware – I really hope you are – but prices for SSDs, USB storage, SD cards, and yet more notable storage components are exponentially higher than ever before. If, like me, you need these to keep a camera running, or maybe store important files, you’ll know the pain of buying any type of storage right now.

Thanks to Anthropic, OpenAI, Google, and more, we’re going to be stuck with shockingly bad prices for a while to come.

According to recent reports, I’ve tried tracking some of the best prices, and while some are still eye-watering, brands like Lexar, PNY, SanDisk, and even Samsung have discounted some of the most popular storage and memory options. I’ve been tracking a few for a while, and sadly, we’re not going to get insane savings, but some are up to 50% off in very rare cases.

Another thing I would advise is to avoid going for huge drives at this stage unless you desperately need it. A 4TB NVMe SSD is going to be steep, and the price per GB starts to get ridiculous. The best deals start to sour once you get past the 1TB range. I wouldn’t recommend an HDD given the speed discrepancies, but maybe for long-term storage you could pick up a larger, slower drive and back up the key content in your life.

Industry observers note that my personal pick for quick, easily accessible storage is the 128GB SanDisk dual USB thumb drive. I’ve used one for several years to transfer files from my phones to PCs and Macs. Fits in your pocket, and although it’s not the fastest, it’s just useful to have a sizable storage device on hand wherever you are. I used to move installation files between my devices, but I’ve even used it as a boot drive when setting up Linux distros on my PCs. It works with Android phones and iPhones too because of the USB-C port. I can’t recommend that one highly enough.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The recent Nvidia saga has had more twists and turns than an Agatha Christie novel.

It all started with Nvidia co-founder and CEO Jensen Huang's admission that he had been unfaithful to his wife. Days later, amid an independent board investigation and broader scrutiny over national-security concerns, he resigned. Less than two weeks later, Huang was back at the helm.

During all of that, Nvidia stock lost over $1 trillion and then regained just under $1 trillion.

The leadership drama has played out at a time when the artificial intelligence market is looking shakier than it has in some time.

Sources indicate that neoclouds have seen stocks plummet in recent months as investors question the sustainability of the AI boom. Chip stocks like Arm and AMD have both fallen in the past month.

Recent findings suggest that huang's surprise return saw Nvidia stock surge 31%, with other AI stocks also gaining. But the sheen was off by Tuesday's close, with Nvidia and a host of chip stocks falling.

The sharp reversal raises questions for investors: did Huang's return restore confidence in Nvidia, or did it spark a short-lived relief rally as the market faces broader questions about returns on AI investment?

Judging by the first few days of his return, it's a hard one to call.

Volatility in the tech sector looked set to continue on Friday, as tech stocks rebounded again.

"Wall Street pared its Monday advance as sobriety returned to the market and a focus returned to fundamentals," wrote Kyle Rodda, analyst at Capital.com, in a note at market close on Tuesday.

"While Jensen Huang's reinstatement as Nvidia CEO is indubitably a boon for the markets and the overall AI trade, it does not assuage every risk and concern about an industry confronting a potential peak in its investment boom and moderating earnings growth.".

The early week rally was "largely driven" by Huang's return, said Violeta Todorova, senior research analyst at Leverage Shares.

In a recent development, "Fresh tariff threats from the Trump administration have added to market uncertainty," she added. "The short-term rally has reversed course, and Nvidia's share price is likely to trade sideways between $125 and $170 in the near term.".

Nvidia stock closed at $149.30 on Wednesday, giving it a $3.6 trillion market cap — a figure around $2 trillion lighter than it was at its peak in October.

"We expect a selective recovery across the AI ecosystem, and NVDA to trade sideways and stay volatile below its October peak at least until the Dec 1–3 Congressional appearances," Egor Tolmachev, senior analyst at Freedom Capital Markets, remarked in a note on Wednesday.

Other key AI stocks have also been volatile. Anthropic's first week as a public company has been mixed. AMD has fallen 25% in the past five days, and memory chip maker Micron has dropped 18%. Both spiked on Monday before paring gains.

The Huang evangelists might've been hoping for a speedier return to AI boom times.

But while the Nvidia CEO's return has removed one source of uncertainty around the chip giant, the volatility among AI stocks suggests investors are still trading on questions much bigger than who occupies the chief executive's office.

Tech German software major SAP is reportedly weighing cutting at least 10,000 jobs in AI push.

According to recent reports, U.S. adds Megaspeed to trade blacklist over export control concerns amid Nvidia controversy.

Robots could be doing household chores in just 1-2 years, a Chinese EV firm states.

SpaceX, Musk pledge to donate a share each to active Trump Accounts.

Jensen Huang tells staff that Nvidia doesn't need a succession plan, according to people inside the room.

Jensen Huang is back as the CEO of Nvidia, and is now tasked with selling the tech giant's AI vision while also defending himself in Washington, my colleague Kif Leswing wrote on Tuesday.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that COPENHAGEN, Denmark—If we lived in the world that Volvo’s product planners expected back when the current XC90 debuted in 2015, both it and the smaller but related XC60 (which arrived in 2017) might have been the last of their kind as everything went electric.
  • It has been revealed that so instead, Volvo has given the XC60 and XC90 another lifecycle refresh.
  • It has been revealed that instead, the Swedish automaker’s attention has been on bringing the technology up to date for model year 2028 standards.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that COPENHAGEN, Denmark—If we lived in the world that Volvo’s product planners expected back when the current XC90 debuted in 2015, both it and the smaller but related XC60 (which arrived in 2017) might have been the last of their kind as everything went electric. As we know, the future hasn’t turned out quite like that, especially in the critically important US market. At the same time, Europe and China are electrifying, which seems like an argument against spending resources on developing all-fresh replacements for models that might not have an eight-year lifespan in most markets.

It has been revealed that so instead, Volvo has given the XC60 and XC90 another lifecycle refresh. The exterior styling tweaks are minimal; the bigger three-row XC90 had already been given a fresh look last year, and the XC60 now gains a similar grille and the same matrix headlights, for instance. And that’s no bad thing—both were, and remain, handsome shapes that are popular with Volvo’s customer base.

It has been revealed that instead, the Swedish automaker’s attention has been on bringing the technology up to date for model year 2028 standards. Which means a much bigger battery for the PHEVs, with sufficient capacity for a couple of days of daily driving for most of us before needing to be recharged. There’s also latest, modern infotainment and interiors that are now even nicer to spend time in than before.

We first saw the revamped 2028 XC60 (and learned about its technical details and those of the XC90) in September, but with the cars going into production now and due to reach the first US customers in the first quarter of next year, we got the opportunity to spend some seat time with the updated cars.

Both the midsize XC60 and three-row XC90 use the same PHEV powertrain. Under the hood, there’s a 2.0 L four-cylinder direct-injection gasoline engine that generates 247 hp (184 kW) and 226 lb-ft (306 Nm) together with a 70 hp (50 kW), 122 ft-lb (165 Nm) electric motor, both of which drive the front wheels. At the rear axle there’s a second electric motor, with an output of 174 hp (130 kW) and 228 lb-ft (309 Nm). Combined output for the hybrid system is 455 hp (339 kW) and 560 lb-ft (759 Nm).

There’s also a much bigger battery, with a net capacity of 37.9 kWh (41.2 kWh gross). If you set the car’s mode to Pure, which relies solely on the rear electric motor for propulsion, that translates to an EPA range estimate of 78 miles (126 km) for the XC60 and 73 miles (116 km) for the larger, draggier XC90. Which is significant—when the average driver drives fewer than 30 miles a day, it means these PHEVs carry enough electrons for a couple of days of tailpipe-emissions-free driving before it needs to be plugged in again or the engine to fire up.

When it is time to plug it back in, expect it to take about four hours with a level 2 charger of at least 16 A, or 27 hours if you’re limited to 120 V. In Hybrid mode, where you get the benefit of both electric motors and the gas engine, Volvo expects a combined efficiency of 67 mpge in the XC60, and 61 mpge for the XC90.

Industry observers note that even if the gas engine is running and you’re in Hybrid or Power mode (which keeps the engine on all the time), you can drive these Volvos as if they were EVs with one-pedal driving: just move the transmission from D to B. The Volvos are always using their electric motors to slow the car before the friction brakes intervene, and in B you get the same amount of lift-off regen regardless of mode. For city traffic, it’s very effective. (In Pure, although only the rear motor deploys energy, both front and rear motors regen brake.).

In power mode, with all 455 hp unleashed, you can chirp the wheels on a wet day, but these model year 2028 cars are about one large male human heavier than the outgoing model year, both of which were already pretty heavy. So don’t expect performance-car performance. The XC60 is the sweeter to drive on a winding road, but both are entirely at home cruising on a highway or creeping along in a city, which is where cars like these spend the vast majority of their time. There’s more road intrusion into the cabin of the XC60—the larger Volvo rides on air suspension that does a much better job of filtering that out.

A first-drive event like this isn’t the best place to get a good read on real-world efficiency. We usually have to share cars with other journalists, and there’s limited time to drive on roads that may not be representative—too sinuous, or not enough traffic, for example. We need to try all the different drive modes and see how cars respond to different inputs. And it’s rare you’ll spend the entire day with one car, finishing at the same point you started.

Recent findings suggest that that remarked, I can’t give you a definite read on range and efficiency for these two plug-ins. But my unscientific estimate is that my drive partner and I, in an XC60, drove about 60 km in a mix of city driving and higher speeds on the way to Malmo in Sweden, which is on the other side of a gigantic bridge, and we used about half the battery pack to do so. (Volvo asked us to put the PHEVs in Hold or Charge mode at 50 percent to leave some state of charge for whoever drove the cars after lunch.).

Industry observers note that thus, there was little charge left in the XC90 when it was my turn to drive the final stint back into Copenhagen. Since I wasn’t worried about combined efficiency, I ran the car in Charge mode for about 20 min, regenerating the battery from an indicated 10 km to an indicated 21 km, then switched to Pure once we reached the city, with about 16 km to go.

Volvo already had a reputation for great automotive interiors, and with this refresh, it has pushed things forward a little. There’s a new wood finish, new textiles, and new backlighting. The resemblance between the two interiors from the front seat is now quite strong, particularly since the test cars Volvo brought to Denmark wore identical color schemes inside.

Our final 1.6 km to the hotel took more than 30 minutes to negotiate thanks to a reception for very important people that apparently took place next to the hotel. Most of this jam was on one street, with our destination in sight, but the frustration was in part ameliorated by Volvo’s secret weapon: its seat massage function.

It has been revealed that lots of other OEMs offer massaging front seats, which inflate and deflate the internal air bladder to massage your shoulders, back, and sometimes butt. But none massage you with quite the firmness of a Volvo seat. And they have the power to distract you from terrible in-car situations, as I discovered when stuck in a V90 Cross Country with Nigel the Cat, whose way of remonstrating with me about his trip to the feline ophthalmologist was to scream at high volume until he ran out of breath, at which point he’d pant for a few minutes, then start again. The seat in that car is the only reason we both made it home safely. And so, in Copenhagen, I set the seat to pulse and did some box breathing.

According to recent reports, as well as new interior materials, you’ll also notice a new infotainment screen in both cars. Gone are the old 9-inch displays, replaced by a new 11.2-inch touchscreen that stands a little proud of the dash rather than recessed into it. Just this one upgrade alone really lifts both interiors; the old, small screen was showing its age. Most Ars readers will recoil at the news that Gemini has replaced the previous Google Assistant, but at least the voice-recognition capabilities are improved. Gemini will still struggle with some commands—I asked it to tell me my current efficiency, which it failed at, but it’s rather good at looking stuff up on the Internet while I drive.

There are also some updated advanced driver-assistance systems, like a warning if cyclists approach your opening door, and an updated 360-degree parking view. But there’s no point-to-point assist like Mercedes is introducing, or a hands-free “level 2+” system like Super Cruise; Volvo’s experience with the EX90 may have left it a little gun-shy.

It has been revealed that with a battery massive enough for daily driving and a more modern interior experience, there’s a lot to like about both the 2029 XC60 and XC90. However, we still don’t know how much they’ll cost when they go on sale in Q1 next year. With twice the battery capacity, it’s reasonable to expect a slight price rise, but without knowing how much, it’s hard to say whether it’s a good deal or not.

Books, bikes, and The Burbs: These are Ars staff’s holiday gift picks for 2026

💡 Key Takeaways
