📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that the holiday shopping season is upon us, and as is our custom, we’re here with a list of Ars staffers’ favorite recent purchases that could make good gifts. (Or maybe they might be a gift you get yourself!).

It has been revealed that rather than try to write a definitive “best gifts for your sister or brother” type of guide, we simply polled Ars staffers on stuff they’ve actually bought this year that they recommend. The thinking is that if we’re into it, hopefully some of you or your friends or family might be. As such, there’s no rhyme or reason to these selections, really; it’s just a list of stuff we bought that we’re happy about. It’s heavy on interesting books and cycling accessories, but there are some gadgets and the like in here, too.

It has been revealed that for each gadget (or whatever else it might be), we have a brief description of how or why we’ve been using this particular thing and why we would recommend it. Our picks are ordered by price, from lowest to highest. Note, though, that the prices of these products are listed as they were when the list was written. Online retailers often adjust prices frequently, especially around Black Friday, so just a heads up: The price might be different by the time you read this.

Also, a callout to the Ars commentariat: If you have your own holiday buying recommendations, feel free to share them. We or some fellow readers might take your advice if you suggest something good! Happy holidays!

Dungeon Crawler Carl by Matt Dinniman – $13.

Recent findings suggest that I understand the convenience and space-savings that e-readers bring. My 2011 Kindle Touch goes with me everywhere I carry my travel backpack, but I’m still a softy for physical books when I’m sitting at home on a lazy Sunday. What started as something of a fanfic send-up of LitRPGs has promptly blossomed into a massive sensation of a series filled with far more depth, heart, and character than the initial premise might indicate. Author Matt Dinniman has an accessible style that will grip any reader with a taste for whimsical adventure. Just be warned that if you leave the books under the tree, you might not see much of the recipient until Newly introduced Year’s.

Undersea War: The Battle to Control the Cables and Pipelines That Connect Our World by Elisabeth Braw– $30.

According to recent reports, lightning Beneath the Sea: The Race to Wire the World and the Dawn of the Information Age by James M. Tabor– $32.

According to recent reports, two excellent books that help describe how the Internet’s undersea backbone became a globe-spanning reality were published in 2026. Together, they form a great gift pairing for anyone interested in how humanity first achieved near-instantaneous communication across the world’s oceans—and how the first trans-Atlantic telegraph cable paved the way for a global network of subsea data cables that now faces growing risks from geopolitical conflicts.

James Tabor’s Lightning Beneath the Sea dives into the astounding real-life story of how American entrepreneur Cyrus Field, lacking in expertise but driven by personal fervor, set out to achieve peace on Earth by laying a 2,000-mile telegraph cable made of copper across the Atlantic seafloor in 1866.

Industry observers note that to pull off the feat, Field managed to convince some of the greatest innovators and scientific luminaries of his day, such as Samuel F.B. Morse, Lord Kelvin, and Michael Faraday, to join his venture. He also refitted the SS Great Eastern steamship, the largest passenger liner ship built to date, as a cable-laying vessel.

That first ocean-spanning telegraph cable gave rise to more such cables for transmitting messages around the world. Eventually copper gave way to a network of subsea fiber-optic cables that became the Internet’s undersea backbone, and the modern world also became interlinked with submarine power cables and underwater pipelines for carrying oil and gas.

Industry observers note that but all that undersea infrastructure is now facing growing danger from the threat of deliberate sabotage, as described in Elisabeth Braw’s book Undersea War. Her book provides a sobering but enlightening look at why subsea cables and pipelines are becoming more tempting targets amid rising geopolitical tensions and conflicts—and how governments and companies are responding to recent cable-cutting incidents around the world.

Read Ars Technica’s Q&A with Elisabeth Braw about Undersea War.

The Burbs Collector’s Edition 4K Blu-ray – $32.

It’s a little-remembered film for most people, but I absolutely love The Burbs. Sure, it’s more Halloween fare than Christmas, but last year I picked The Thing, so clearly “1980s movies for October” is my December viewing MO.

Starring Tom Hanks, Carrie Fisher, and Corey Feldman, this is a dry, hilarious send-up of suburban life with a horror-adjacent mystery that keeps you guessing. (It’s not scary, though.) I hardly ever hear anyone else talk about this movie, but I love it, and it only recently came out in 4K, so I’m taking this opportunity to shout it out.

How Apollo Flew to the Moon by David Woods – $35.

Sources indicate that if you’re a technically minded Ars reader looking for a nice book to snuggle down with over the holidays, David Woods’ How Apollo Flew to the Moon could be just the thing. (There’s also an audiobook version.) Woods has an accessible style that breaks down complex engineering challenges and their solutions into easily digestible chunks that clarify without oversimplifying. He uses that style to take readers on a detailed trip through the machinery of Project Apollo, from the launch facilities and Mission Control all the way to the specific mechanics of how to navigate to and land on the Moon—and, from there, how to return safely to Earth.

Ever wondered about the insane engineering that let the Saturn V’s first stage burn almost 15 tons of fuel every second as it powered the crew into orbit? Or how to pinpoint a spacecraft’s centimeter-precise distance from Earth on its way to the Moon? Or how Apollo crews tracked their own position with stellar navigation, using sextants and star sightings? Or what a REFSMMAT is, or how television transmissions from the Moon worked, or how they got those crazy lunar buggies onto the Moon’s surface? All these questions and more are given beautifully complete and technically satisfying answers, suitable for both the curious layperson and also the interested engineer. Grab this book and stun your family at Christmas with amazing Apollo trivia—as a bonus, you’ll have the knowledge to make your “We never landed on the Moon!” conspiracy theorist uncle so angry that he stops talking and watches football in grumpy silence! Everyone wins!

According to recent reports, as someone who grew up in the classic era of 16-bit SNES RPGs, this 40th anniversary tribute to the series’ history is everything I could have ever wanted in a modern entry. I haven’t properly played through a Final Fantasy entry since the days of Final Fantasy X on PlayStation 2, but when friends kept nudging me that this was the perfect “Nick game,” I figured I should probably take a look. There’s a free six-hour demo available on supported platforms if you’re still on the fence about picking this one up, but don’t be surprised if you end up grabbing a copy for yourself.

Govee Star Light Projector (Nebula Effect) – $70.

It has been revealed that for the past couple of years, I’ve been transforming my tiny office into a sanctuary in the evenings, since I do most of my writing (and gaming) in here then. It started with Govee Hexa panels, then came an RGB TV backlight, then colorful smart bulbs for the built-in light fixtures. I topped it off with the Star Light projector, which coats the ceiling in a soothing, ever-shifting, immersive stars-and-nebula effect.

It has been revealed that it’s probably not for everybody, but my office is tiny, and I spend a lot of time here both for work and for fun. Tapping a button to completely shift the vibe is surprisingly effective at making it a room I don’t mind spending time in even after I’ve been working in it all day.

In a recent development, easily my favorite impulse purchase of 2026, the FM-1 is a great gift for curious tinkerers and experienced musicians alike. At around $70 or less, you don’t have to break the bank to get fiddling. A perfectly decent stock synthesizer on its own, the real fun starts when you begin experimenting with the community firmware packages that transform the synth into anything from a multi-track groovebox to one of the more hilarious ways that I’ve ever tried to play Doom.

Sources indicate that trek BellBeats digital bike bell and speaker – $125One of the great things about cycling is the chance to be alone with my thoughts—just me and my bike. But that can be too much of a good thing on longer zone 2 rides and centuries. Sporting the size and shape of an old-school bicycle bell, the Trek BellBeats is a safer alternative to donning headphones while on the bike.BellBeats pair with your phone via Bluetooth and will play music at a volume loud enough to enjoy your tunes or hear navigation prompts, but they are not so loud that the music drowns out traffic (or the radar on your bike computer). They can be mounted on just about any non-aero handlebars, charge over USB-C, and offer up to six hours of playtime. And as a bonus, they double as a bicycle bell.

I use Bluetooth headphones most of the time, but frustratingly, they don’t work with voice chat on the PlayStation 5, and I needed a good-quality headset for my Friday night multiplayer gaming sessions.

According to recent reports, I’ve always liked Fractal Design’s PC cases, so I decided to roll the dice on their affordable-for-the-quality, over-ear headphones. They support Bluetooth, but they also have a USB dongle, so they can be used for voice chat on game consoles, too.

Recent findings suggest that I was surprised by how much I like them, and despite buying them just for the PS5, I’ve ended up using them in other contexts. Part of that is because they’re very comfortable, and the design avoids my glasses frames well.

I also like that, although they are gaming headphones with all the expected bells and whistles for that, they don’t have an over-the-top design.

If you’re in the market for mid-range wireless gaming headphones that look like something you could actually wear in public without embarrassment, these fit the bill so far.

In a recent development, povec C1 Performance Sunglasses – $250Photochromic sunglasses are incredibly useful for outdoor workouts. Two of the most popular bike trails near me run through forest preserves, and the lighting changes steadily as the forest canopy closes in or spreads out. My default sunglasses are a cheap, $28 pair from Rockbros.Unlike other photochromic glasses, which change tints via a pokey chemical reaction, the Povec C1 uses a battery to switch between tints in a second. All the rider (or runner) needs to do is swipe the right temple and the lenses will darken or lighten almost instantaneously. The C1 charges via a small USB-C port, and the Povec claims 28 days of battery life with four hours of daily usage. I’ve used them off and on for about six weeks and have only had to charge them once.

The C1 comes in three frame colors and either Green Revo or Gold Revo glasses and is an excellent stocking stuffer for the runner, cyclist, or skier in your life.

Garmin Varia RCT715 radar camera tail light – $300Last spring, a friend of mine was the victim of a hit-and-run while on a ride. Although she wasn’t seriously hurt, her brand-new bike was totaled. The driver got an unwelcome surprise a couple of days later when the police knocked on his front door and arrested him. My friend was riding with a Garmin Varia RCT715, a combination taillight and radar with a camera. The 1080p/30 fps camera captured the car’s license plate, making it possible for the police to identify the driver.More than 90 percent of my riding is on roads, and I don’t feel fully comfortable without my Varia. I have it paired with my Garmin Edge 1050 bike computer, but it will work with most other brands via ANT+. The Varia detects approaching vehicles at 140 meters, and I have it set to record video starting when a car is detected and for 30 seconds after it passes. Battery life is up to six hours, depending on whether the taillight is solid or flashing, and video is saved on a 16GB microSD memory card.

Hiplock DX1000 Bike Lock – $380.

My YouTube algorithm has recently fed me videos of testers using an angle grinder to cut through decent bike locks in under a minute. I’ve never seen an angle grinder-assisted theft in person, but I’ve seen enough heaps of bike parts around town to know people’s rides are getting jacked somewhere. As someone known to be neurotic about leaving my bike outside my purview, I’m looking for added security measures to ease my stress.Enter the Hiplok, which, according to the tests I’ve watched, will turn multiple angle-grinder blades to dust. Do bike thieves carry several discs, and will they spend about 15 minutes trying to break this lock? I don’t know, but I have my doubts. At nearly $400, it’s about as expensive as it gets to secure your ride, but when your bike tops $5,000, it’s probably worth the added theft deterrence and peace of mind.

Santa left this one last year, and the rest of my handheld collection has felt neglected since. Sporting a Snapdragon 8 Elite (now dubbed the Dragonwing Q8) chip, excellent ergonomics, and a 6-inch 120Hz AMOLED screen, it’s the perfect balance between size and horsepower. The Android unit is capable enough to play most anything you can throw at it, without the bulk of a Steam Deck or the bloat of a Windows handheld. Thanks to things like Proton, FEX translation, and software like DroidDeck or GameNative, there isn’t much I can’t use it for. Streaming consoles or PC gaming? Check. Access to Steam, GOG, Epic, Rockstar libraries? Check. High-end native Android gaming? Yup. Emulate anything under the sun? You’re covered there, too. The latest Odin 3 Portal hardware revision gets a larger 7-inch screen and a base RAM configuration of 12GB over the original model’s 8GB. I may have to ask Mr. Claus about an upgrade….

More significant to me personally, the upgrade also seems to have fixed a longstanding CarPlay bug regarding playlist sorting.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, the message from the Trump administration to one of the world’s leading semiconductor companies was clear: Give the US government a chunk of your firm. Right now. Or else.

Recent findings suggest that do not make the “mistake of thinking that this is a negotiation,” Commerce Department lawyer David Shapiro told the chief financial officer of the Intel Corporation in August 2025, according to internal notes from a company call contained in a federal lawsuit. “The President is expecting to announce a deal on these terms on Friday.”.

Shapiro acknowledged that “the Board could choose not to accept the offer,” according to a summary of his remarks prepared for Intel’s directors. But the Trump administration official “noted that rejection will have consequences that [Shapiro] cannot predict.”.

Days later, the board gave the administration what it wanted. “It is my Great Honor to report that the United States of America now fully owns and controls 10% of INTEL,” Donald Trump posted to his social platform. “The United States paid nothing for these Shares, and the Shares are now valued at approximately $11 Billion Dollars. This is a great Deal for America.”.

Sources indicate that president Trump was similarly jubilant on Monday, announcing that he had “convinced” Nvidia’s board of directors to rehire chief executive Jensen Huang. The proclamation was a shock. But it wasn’t entirely without precedent.

Industry observers note that fifteen months earlier, the Trump administration had interfered with the leadership decisions at another major chipmaker, court documents allege. Then, as now, allegations swirled that the company’s CEO was too close to China. Then, as now, the Trump administration dealt itself into the company’s financial future.

It’s part of a broader shift within the government in general and the Commerce Department in particular, a former member of that department tells WIRED. Out are old metrics “like creating jobs or the US being more competitive or owning more of the market share,” this ex-Trump administration official claims. When dealing with private companies, a single overriding concern is: “Are you going to give back to the government in cash?”.

According to recent reports, documents unredacted as part of a shareholder’s lawsuit against Intel’s board show how far the administration has been willing to go to get what it wants. The lawsuit’s allegations were previously reported by WP Intelligence.

“The Board, operating under the shadow of the President’s threats,” the lawsuit alleges, “caved to the government’s extortion.” A second case, asking for internal records, was filed in April by the same shareholder, Richard Paisner, against Nvidia.

“It’s just straight-up coercion,” says Scott Lincicome, a vice president at the libertarian Cato Institute. “The firm starts making decisions not based on what’s best for the company in the short or long term, what’s best for shareholders, but what’s best for politics and what the government is demanding.”.

Recent findings suggest that “That’s not what you want from any company,” he adds. “When you’re talking about the world’s most innovative companies and these kinds of bleeding-edge technologies that have not only huge economic implications but national security ones, then that’s a huge problem.”.

In a recent development, representatives for Intel declined to comment for this story. The White House, Commerce Department, and Nvidia did not respond to requests for comment.

The parallels between Nvidia’s government-assisted autogolpe and Intel’s alleged forced sale aren’t exact. In the Intel case, Trump all but accused the firm’s boss of being compromised by Beijing; in the Nvidia situation, the president reportedly dismissed concerns from his own intelligence agencies about the executive’s connections to China. But both instances show a growing fusion of private enterprise and public office.

During the Biden administration, Intel won awards for up to $11 billion in government grants and contracts, much of it under the CHIPS Act, which was meant to help build semiconductor manufacturing and assembly plants in America and bolster domestic research.

It has been revealed that at the time, there was some grumbling inside the Commerce Department, which administered the CHIPS and Science Act grants, about funding what was seen as a “failing incumbent” in the semiconductor space, states the former official. (Intel had, in recent years, fallen on hard times.) But by March 2025, Intel had received about $2.2 billion of the grants. That’s when President Trump told Congress that the CHIPS Act was “a horrible, horrible thing.” The rest of Intel’s money was put on hold, tied to hitting certain milestones, while the administration stated it was renegotiating the deals.

In a recent development, the same month Lip-Bu Tan was hired as Intel’s new CEO. Soon after, his ties to China made him a Trump target, when Reuters reported that Tan had invested in “hundreds of Chinese tech firms,” some with connections to Beijing’s military. Tan’s former firm, Cadence Design Systems, pleaded guilty to violating US sanctions by selling semiconductor designs to a restricted Chinese military university, and agreed to pay more than $140 million in fines. Tan was never personally charged, but the violations happened while he was the CEO.

According to recent reports, two weeks later, the president was watching Maria Bartiromo’s show on the Fox Business Network. It mentioned a letter a senator had sent Intel about the China ties. Trump posted, “The CEO of INTEL is highly CONFLICTED and must resign, immediately. There is no other solution to this problem.”.

In a recent development, tan went to the Oval Office on August 11 to see if there was, in fact, another solution. He got 40 minutes with the president, Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick, and Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent.

Tan claimed his experience in China was a strength, not a detriment. According to the book Regime Change, Tan argued that there was no way he could’ve known about every one of the deals his many companies made; Trump, who had his own sprawling business empire, surely knew what that was like. Tan promised to give up his holdings in China, according to a letter Tan shared with Intel’s board, and put any proceeds into a blind trust.

In a recent development, “The primary goal was to eliminate any worries about Lip-Bu himself, his Cadence background, and his investments with China,” according to a source with knowledge of the matter. But there were major financial concerns for Intel, too. “We had declining revenues and needed money.”.

Sources indicate that neither Tan’s letter, excerpted in the complaint, nor Trump’s social media posts praising the CEO after the meeting mentioned anything about giving the government a chunk of the tech giant. Yet Trump later insisted that a deal had been cooked up right then and there. “He came in, he saw me, we talked for a while. I liked him a lot, I thought he was very good,” the president told The Wall Street Journal. “I mentioned, ‘You know what? I think the United States should be given 10% of Intel.’ And he said, ‘I would consider that.’”.

“I should’ve asked for more. It was so easy,” Trump later recalled.

Industry observers note that according to the court filing’s review of Intel’s internal documents, Shapiro—a former partner at the Fresh York law firm Wachtell, Lipton, Rosen & Katz—made a verbal offer on August 18. Ultimately, in exchange for the cut of Intel, the Trump administration would free up the $8.9 billion US government grants that it had already won. They wanted about a tenth of the manufacturer’s stock for free, in exchange for Washington keeping the commitment it had already made.

In a recent development, then came the call in which Shapiro insisted there was no room for negotiation. “The board needs to consider,” he said, according to Intel’s summary of his remarks included in the court documents, the “benefits of having a friend in this administration and what the administration can do to help Intel (including with customers).”.

Recent findings suggest that intel’s board met, and decided they hated the deal. “The economic terms that had been proposed [by] the Administration were not, in their current form, attractive to the company,” minutes of the meeting, reprinted in the lawsuit, noted.

But they went ahead with it anyway. Paisner’s lawyers say in the court documents the board took the offer thrust forward by the administration. Intel’s attorneys disagree, arguing in their motion to dismiss that there was some back-and-forth deal-making, and it made the agreement more favorable to the tech giant. The grants became “immediately available” while “strategically aligning the interests of Intel’s stockholders and the US Government.”.

On August 25, Lutnick released a video with Tan, sitting side-by-side on cushioned chairs. “I really look forward to have the US government be my shareholder,” Tan turned to Lutnick and remarked. “And we can work together and make Intel great again.”.

Industry observers note that inside the tech giant, the video was “a surprise to everyone,” according to a source with direct knowledge of the matter. Some employees joked that it was reminiscent of a “hostage video.”.

Industry observers note that not long after that, Nvidia—led by Tan’s friend Jensen Huang—made a $5 billion investment in Intel. “I love seeing their stock price go up, making the USA RICHER, AND RICHER,” Trump posted. “Who would not want to make deals like that?”.

Industry observers note that deals, plural. On the day Tan was hauled to the Oval Office, Trump declared that his administration had been negotiating separately with Huang. The Nvidia leader was beyond eager to sell more of his semiconductors to China. “And I mentioned, if I’m going to do that, I want you to pay us as a country something,’” Trump said. They settled on 15 percent of all sales of the H20 model chip. Months after that, they cut a second deal: a 25 percent bounty on sales of Nvidia’s even-more advanced H200 chips.

In their lawsuit against Nvidia, Paisner’s attorneys argue the surcharges amount to “unlawful taxes,” and that the board’s “decisions to enter into such agreements are the product of mismanagement and breaches of fiduciary duty.”.

It has been revealed that in court, NVIDIA’s lawyers insisted that the firm “did not enter into any illegal ‘agreement’ with the government but instead engaged with the government and stated that it would comply with federal regulations.” Moreover, the attorneys say Paisner is trying to make a political point, rather than a legal one. “When asked about his purpose in bringing this action,” they write, “Paisner was candid: ‘It’s to make a public point of how NVIDIA conducts itself.’”.

The attorneys wrote this in May, months before Nvidia’s and Huang’s recent drama. Last week, board chair Harvey Jones mentioned on the company’s quarterly earnings call that it did “not intend to reinstate Jensen as CEO,” citing his “disclosure of personal behavior inconsistent with the company’s code of conduct, standards, and cultural norms.” (Not to mention mounting evidence that the company’s most sophisticated chips were making their way to China, in violation of US law.) But, according to The Fresh York Times, after days of pressure from top administration officials, the company and the government essentially struck a deal Sunday night to reinstate Huang.

It has been revealed that “Don’t think for a second that politics ever play a role in this firm, not even a little bit,” Huang remarked during his first company-wide meeting after rejoining the company, WIRED reported. “We are the most apolitical company. I don’t love that we talk about politics here. Take it home. I love that we talk about work here.”.

Additional reporting by Lauren Goode.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Following new regulations, Google Play will require Android app developers to publicly post a business address starting in 2027 and, while there are workarounds, it’s not going to be the easiest thing.

It has been revealed that latest Digital Services Act regulations in the EU and UK will require developers to share a phone number and address publicly. While this is only required in those regions, this information will be visible worldwide. Google does not allow PO boxes to be used for this requirement, meaning that many smaller developers will be left with limited options beyond posting their own personal address.

Exceptions to the rule include apps that are not published in the UK or Europe, or developes that qualify as “non-traders” which is essentially those making no money off of their apps.

Here’s how Google defines a “trader” in the context of Android apps:.

The Verge notes that a “registered agent service” can be used as a business address for those who don’t have a physical office, and that Apple is allowing iOS developers to use a PO box if they prove the box is linked to a physical address.

According to recent reports, google will require Android app developers to confirm their trader status and their address by February 1, 2027. Account-wide status can be found in the Google Play Console via Manage account > Account details > About you, while status on a per-app basis can be handled via Monitor and improve > Policy and programs > App content.

Industry News: Google will soon share Android developers' addresses publicly

📅 27 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (324 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Engadget

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Their phone numbers and addresses will be published globally, starting on March 1, 2027.
  • According to recent reports, starting on March 1, 2027, Google will display Android developers' phone numbers and addresses with their apps, and users everywhere will be able to see them.
  • Recent findings suggest that google, like Apple, now requires developers to declare whether they're a trader under UK laws and the European Union's Digital Services Act (DSA).

Their phone numbers and addresses will be published globally, starting on March 1, 2027.

According to recent reports, starting on March 1, 2027, Google will display Android developers' phone numbers and addresses with their apps, and users everywhere will be able to see them. As The Elec has reported, this decision has been met with criticism, specifically from smaller developers who operate out of their homes. Some of them have been opting to rent offices just so they won't have to declare their real address. "Disclosing developers' home addresses amounts to an invasion of privacy," one independent developer told the publication.

Recent findings suggest that google, like Apple, now requires developers to declare whether they're a trader under UK laws and the European Union's Digital Services Act (DSA). The manufacturer says they have to classify themselves as a trader if they intend to earn money from their apps in any way on a regular basis, and if they already have a consistent frequency of transactions. Developers will have to make their declaration by February 1, 2027. Once they classify themselves as a trader, they'll have to submit their business identity, phone number and address, which Google will display to consumers everywhere. Users in the UK and the European Economic Area will also see their business details and self-certification.

In a recent development, if they fail to comply with these requirements, Google could block their updates from rolling out. Ultimately, the organization could remove their apps from the Play store, not just in Europe, but in all regions around the world. The Verge notes that Google doesn't accept PO Boxes for an address like Apple does, forcing people to think of ways to protect their identifying information while still earning money from their apps. Apple also won't be displaying developers' phone numbers and addresses globally like Google intends to do, only in the European countries covered by the laws requiring them.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Elon Musk's social network X just got a new feature it never had under previous ownership.

That would be parental controls for teen customers, to be exact. In a upcoming post from the official Safety account on X, the company revealed it has implemented parental controls for users aged 13 to 17. The way it works is that an account run by a parent or guardian establishes a supervisory link to the account run by a teen, which gives the parent or guardian access to a bunch of monitoring and safety features the site didn't have before.

According to recent reports, these features include the ability to monitor usage and set daily limits for the teen, as well as the option to require newly introduced followers to be approved by the parent or guardian. Recommendations on the For You feed can be limited to accounts the teen already follows, while parents can mute specific words, control who can send direct messages, and see who the teens have chatted with in DMs without seeing the messages themselves.

In a recent development, everyone's journey through Grand Theft Auto VI is going to go a little differently, as that's the nature of a big, freeform open-world adventure. But one thing is certain for every player: You're going to need money, and fast.

It has been revealed that that's especially true at the beginning of chapter 2 of the game's main story. For reasons I won't spoil in case you aren't there yet, chapter 2 finds Jason and Lucia in a tough spot with almost no money to their names, and an urgent need to get some. Thankfully, there are a couple of different methods that, when combined, can net you somewhere between $15,000 and $20,000, with almost no killing or even any real effort required.

Just understand that there may be some minor spoilers for the beginning of chapter 2 if you decide to read ahead.

We'll start with a method to get at least $10,000 (and possibly as much as $14,000), which we first learned about from GamingBible and tested ourselves to ensure it worked. Without beating around the bush, it does work.

It involves going to an abandoned warehouse outside the town of Hamlet, which is easily accessible from the very beginning of the game. However, because (spoiler warning) you lose all of your held money at the end of chapter 1, I highly advise waiting until chapter 2 to do this.

Sources indicate that anyway, you'll know you're in the right place if you follow the waypoint marker in the screenshot above and see a warehouse with an Apollo sign out front. It has been revealed that this second batch of cash is one we heard about from our friends at IGN, and, again, we can vouch for it ourselves. It's worth playing a couple of story missions to at least fix the vehicle problem first before doing this next bit of money-stealing.

To be specific, there is a "rainy day fund" of $5,000 cash hidden in Jason's bedroom in his old house. Unfortunately, by this point in the game, that house has been exploded real good, and the entire neighborhood is a heat area where cops are stationed and looking for Jason and Lucia. It's a bit of a hike from where the story takes place in chapter 2, and it's in a risky spot, so this is a super easy wad of cash to miss.

Sources indicate that still, you can at least drive (or take a cab) down to the area outside the heat zone and go on foot from there. Do whatever you can to sneak to the backside of Jason's house and get inside. You can easily evade the cops if you stick to nearby backyards and maybe do a little bit of swimming. Just stay crouched and quiet, and you'll get in and out easily. Once you're in, go to Jason's old bedroom, open the stash, and grab the $5,000. You can also optionally grab some old photos while you're at it, which will raise Jason and Lucia's relationship rating.

Sources indicate that these upcoming features are nice to have, but Active Noise Cancellation is where AirPods Pro 3 become a major upgrade. Apple says it’s “the world’s best in-ear Active Noise Cancellation.” Here’s how the new ANC compares to previous models:.

Sources indicate that I spend nearly my entire workday with AirPods Pro 3 in my ears. Whether I’m working from home with young kids around or at a busy coffee shop, I rely on ANC to block out background noise and help me focus.

Sources indicate that one reason I’ve been especially impressed with the ANC upgrades is that I didn’t have any real complaints about ANC on AirPods Pro 2. But Apple managed to deliver improvements in AirPods Pro 3 I had no idea I needed, and when I’ve tried going back to AirPods Pro 2 I couldn’t believe how much noise was let in.

If Active Noise Cancellation is key to you, I highly recommend AirPods Pro 3.

iOS 27.3 is coming soon, and it’s a significant revision for upcoming iPhone features, including additions that span six built-in Apple apps. Here’s what’s new.

Apple Music adds a pair of upgrades in iOS 27.3. Selfie Sing is an all-new feature that lets you record short videos of yourself singing along to your favorite songs, aided by onscreen lyrics. It’s perfect for sharing on TikTok or other social platforms.

If you’re not the type to share karaoke videos online, another nice iOS 27.3 change is that the lyrics view for songs has gotten an iPhone Duo-inspired upgrade in landscape mode. Now, artwork for the song you’re listening to blends beautifully into the stream of lyrics.

Read more: iOS 27.3 upgrades Apple Music in two ways, here’s what’s new.

Safari is getting several exciting newly introduced features in iOS 27.3, including:.

Read more: iOS 27.3 and macOS 27.3 add Vertical Tabs, Adaptive Dark Mode, and more to Safari.

Apple’s Health app gets a major overhaul in iOS 27.3, though only for Apple Intelligence-compatible iPhones.

The new Health app has an Insights tab for personalized data visualization and guidance, Longevity tab for tracking your health age, and there are new features like educational videos, movement evaluations, and the ability to order labs that get automatically imported into the app.

Read more: iOS 27.3 adds all-latest Apple Health app, details here.

Vertical video is coming with a fresh Clips feature that lets you browse short samples of Apple TV shows and movies in a TikTok-style vertically scrolling format.

Video podcasts are also coming to the TV app, with the option to automatically sync playback from Apple Podcasts inside the TV app.

Read more: iOS 27.3 brings vertical video and video podcasts to Apple TV app.

Apple Fitness+ is getting a massive expansion in iOS 27.3 with a new Gym Strength program.

Gym Strength lets you build a strength program that fits your schedule and the equipment you have on hand. It’s fully customizable and provides Apple’s best offering yet for traditional strength training.

Whether you’re brand new to strength training or just benefit from some additional structure, Gym Strength is a great reason to try out Fitness+.

Read more: Apple reveals Fitness+ Gym Strength program with personalized workout looks.

Industry observers note that apple’s Freeform app gets a handful of improvements in iOS 27.3, including newly introduced text styling options and preset background colors to choose from. You can also generate custom shapes using Apple Intelligence.

Support for storing your driver’s license in Apple Wallet has gradually been expanding across the United States. Today, we have a status upgrade on when the feature will go live in Connecticut, which Apple has touted as a planned partner since September 2021.

9to5Mac is sponsored by Sony: Score Sony’s INZONE noise-canceling earbuds for 38% off. These deliver immersive 360 Spatial Sound, active noise canceling, low-latency wireless connectivity, and much more.

Industry observers note that last week, Connecticut released its own mobile ID app for iPhone on the App Store, but without Apple Wallet support. As spotted by MacRumors, however, the app’s developer indicates that Apple Wallet support is “coming soon.”.

While the state and developer haven’t shared any more specific information recently, a press release in May from Connecticut Governor Ned Lamont noted the goal is to expand digital wallet ID support to Apple Wallet, Google Wallet, and Samsung Wallet by August 2027.

Connecticut residents have been waiting a long time for the state to launch Apple Wallet ID support. This is the first notable revision we’ve had in a while.

When Apple declared support for storing your driver’s license in Apple Wallet in 2021, the company touted the following partners:.

So three of Apple’s launch partners have yet to roll out support for Apple Wallet IDs. Kentucky previously unveiled that it planned to launch support sometime in the summer, but it has missed that deadline. Evidence found within Apple’s backend code suggests that Utah support should go live soon.

You can use Apple Wallet IDs at TSA checkpoints, as well as at select businesses and organizations in person, in app, and online. It does not replace your physical license. Here are the full details on acceptance.

Apple Wallet support for IDs expanding to additional states isn’t quite as notable as it used to be. Last year, Apple launched a latest Digital ID feature that is powered by your US passport. While it’s not your driver’s license, it’s a way to use your iPhone at TSA checkpoints at more than 250 airports in the United States.

The Google Home app is better than Nest alone ever was, mostly

📅 22 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (799 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: 9to5google

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • The Nest app is officially dead, but it’s worth taking a step back and remembering that, while there are some rough edges, the Google Home app is a better smart home experience than Nest alone ever could have been.
  • In a recent development, the Nest app has been on life support for years now.
  • Realistically, even long-time Nest users have had no reason to continue using the app over Google Home.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The Nest app is officially dead, but it’s worth taking a step back and remembering that, while there are some rough edges, the Google Home app is a better smart home experience than Nest alone ever could have been.

In a recent development, the Nest app has been on life support for years now. Google has been migrating legacy products into the Home app for a while and the last few puzzle pieces came in Nest Protect support, the death of the earliest Nest Thermostats, and other assorted adjustments.

Realistically, even long-time Nest users have had no reason to continue using the app over Google Home.

It has been revealed that having been personally, deeply invested in Google’s vision for the smart home over the past decade, I’ll say that the Google Home app we have today is better than the Nest app ever was or ever could be. A huge part of that comes from Google Home’s ability to pull together devices from third-party ecosystems. Being able to control your entire smart home from a single app is how the smart home always should have been, and between Google’s work and the Matter standard, we’re finally able to enjoy that pretty seamlessly for the most part. Automations, Google’s actually-useful AI features, and more only sweeten the deal. I’m also a major fan of what the Home app has become from a UX perspective. While there are always rough edges and bugs to clean up, the customizable homepage and well-organized sections make for a good – not perfect, but good – experience for the end user.

That said, there is one thing that the Nest app’s limited scope benefitted from, and that’s a focus on making your own product great.

Industry observers note that google’s move to the Home app for Nest devices has been a 5-year run of trying to clean things up, improve on the app, and basically bring back the way things were in the Nest app as far as the first-party cameras and thermostats are concerned. It’s taken ages, but we’re finally up to speed, mostly. I still hate that you have to reset Nest Cams to change Wi-Fi when the Nest app just let you change it, and the Nest app’s settings were much less overwhelming, but I’d say the pros far outweigh the cons at this point.

It has been revealed that the Nest app was good at its job, but the Google Home app is a worthy successor, finally, and now the Nest app can finally rest. I mostly think the same applies to Gemini vs Google Assistant, with the newer assistant a better overall experience, but it’s easier to poke holes in that argument.

Disagree? What do you think of the Google Home app, and were you still using the Nest app?

If you're like me, you put your keys down the second you get into the house and immediately forget where you left them.

That's where smart tags come in: these little trackers tell you exactly where you've put whatever one is attached to and will guide you straight to its location. They can even emit an alarm sound, making it easier to find something that you might have stowed away in a pocket or desk drawer.

Apple's AirTag is a popular choice, but right now mobile accessory maker Ugreen is selling a four-pack of its Android alternative for just $26.99 (down from $33.99) at Amazon as part of its Black Friday sales. That's right, a pack of not one or two but (count 'em) four standalone smart tags that you can attach to your keys, stow in your luggage, and so on. That works out to just under $7 per tag!

The Finder Duo Air Tracker Tags are fully compatible with Google's Find Hub, so you don't need to worry about Android compatibility. Despite being cheaper, they also boast some advantages compared to other trackers. Namely, batteries that you can recharge via USB Type-C and a louder speaker to make them even easier to locate when you need to use the alarm.

In a recent development, these little smart tags are perfect if you keep losing your keys or otherwise want to keep track of your stuff. They're rechargeable via USB-C and fully compatible with Google's Find Hub.

✅Recommended if: You want affordable smart trackers that work well with an Android phone to keep track of your keys or other small objects.

It has been revealed that ❌Skip this deal if: You don't think the trackers will be useful, or you don't need four. If you can't think of anything that you would be likely to lose, then chances are these trackers are not a good investment.

Similarly, if you would rather spend the same amount or more on just a single tracker, then there are other options available.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Workers voted 75 percent against the IWGB recognition agreement.
  • Workers voted 75 percent against the IWGB recognition agreement.
  • Workers at Grand Theft Auto VI developer Rockstar Games won’t unionize, after the vote for a formal recognition agreement failed, with only 25 percent of votes in favor of unionization.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Workers voted 75 percent against the IWGB recognition agreement.

Workers voted 75 percent against the IWGB recognition agreement.

Workers at Grand Theft Auto VI developer Rockstar Games won’t unionize, after the vote for a formal recognition agreement failed, with only 25 percent of votes in favor of unionization. The Independent Workers Union of Great Britain (IWGB) stated that Rockstar workers in the union will continue organizing even without formal recognition.

In a recent development, voting ran from November 12th through 26th, covering the launch of GTA VI. If successful, the vote would have established a formal framework for collective negotiation with the studio over pay, overtime, bonuses, leave, and pensions, along with a right to consultation over future changes including AI implementation and layoffs. Without it, Rockstar won’t have an obligation to meet union representatives, though workers and union members can still lobby for change informally.

“For anyone at Rockstar who believes in a fairer workplace, a fairer sector and a fairer society - this isn’t a sign to retreat, it’s a sign to double down on what we stand for,” IWGB said in a statement sent to The Verge. “Hundreds of our coworkers voted in favour of our union at Rockstar, yet sadly we recognise we have more work to do to build understanding and win the trust of more of our colleagues. We’re ready to put in the effort to make that happen.”.

When Rockstar fired 31 IWGB members last year, the union accused it of “the most blatant and ruthless act of union busting in the history of the games industry.” That case has gone to a UK employment tribunal, with a judgment still pending.

“We are extraordinarily proud of our team, the culture we’ve built together and the launch of Grand Theft Auto VI,” Rockstar head of publishing Jennifer Kolbe told Bloomberg News. “This result reflects our team’s strong support for continuing the direct relationships, collaboration and open dialogue that have helped make Rockstar Games so innovative and strong. As we look ahead, we’re excited to build on all we’ve accomplished together.”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that the Samsung Galaxy Watch Ultra 2 is worth spending more on if you want longer battery life, a brighter outdoor display, and specialized features for trail running and diving. The Galaxy Watch 9 is the better fit if you want Samsung’s latest everyday health tools in a smaller, lighter watch.

It has been revealed that both, however, are fantastic smartwatches with limitless potential. They share a Snapdragon Wear Elite processor and many of Samsung’s newest wellness features, so deciding between them is really about figuring out your priorities when it comes to buying a wearable this holiday season. We’re here to help you figure that out.

This post is sponsored by Samsung.

It has been revealed that as we covered in our Galaxy Watch 9 and Watch Ultra 2 comparison, both watches move to Qualcomm’s Snapdragon Wear Elite platform. Both also ship with Wear OS 7 and One UI 8 Watch.

That shared foundation includes useful health insights. Vitals brings overnight measurements together to establish your personal baseline, while Daily Cardio Load helps you understand training demands and recovery. Hearing monitoring can flag potentially unsafe noise levels, whether you’re at a concert or somewhere unexpectedly loud.

Both also get five years of Wear OS updates and security patches, making either a useful long-term partner for your Samsung device, like the Galaxy S26 Ultra or Galaxy Z Fold8.

It has been revealed that the clearest differences are size, battery capacity, display brightness, and outdoor capabilities. Here’s how the lineup breaks down:.

As you can tell, the Galaxy Watch Ultra 2 is considerably bigger and heavier, but you get a lot more capability for that additional size.

The Galaxy Watch Ultra 2 makes its strongest case when your plans regularly take you beyond a desk, a gym, or a charger.

Samsung rates the Galaxy Watch Ultra 2 for up to 60 hours with the always-on display enabled, compared with up to 30 hours for the Watch 9, and that extra headroom is appealing when your day starts with a workout and finishes well into the evening.

Then there’s the screen. In our hands-on with both watches, the Ultra 2’s brightness stood out immediately, with a higher peak that gives it an advantage when checking workout information outdoors, even in the bright sun. And its titanium frame provides added durability.

Sources indicate that the Ultra 2 also adds Trail Run tracking for elevation and terrain impact, route guidance using compatible GPX files, and Nutrition Alert hydration guidance. These are tangible reasons to upgrade if your usual run involves trails instead of pavement.

Diving is another differentiator. Samsung specifies recreational diving support to depths of up to 40 meters, with automatic tracking of depth, dive time and water temperature — a remarkable feat for a piece of technology that lives on your wrist.

The best choice becomes clearer when you picture your own routine:.

Choose the Galaxy Watch 9 for everyday wellness, a lighter fit, and strong value. Choose the Galaxy Watch Ultra 2 for longer adventures, more demanding outdoor activities, and greater freedom between charges.

Sources indicate that if you’re replacing an older Galaxy Watch, both offer a compelling latest generation of health insights and long-term support. Both last a long time and look absolutely awesome with running shorts or a business suit. But the Watch Ultra 2 can take you that extra mile, literally and figuratively, and may be worth spending more on during Best Buy’s Holiday Deals event.

Hulu offers dramas like Furious, Alien: Earth, The Lowdown, and The Handmaid’s Tale, as well as comedies like Bob’s Burgers, Futurama, and It’s Always Sunny in Philadelphia. Disney Plus, meanwhile, is home to Disney and Pixar favorites, The Simpsons, and a wide selection of Star Wars and Marvel movies and shows. It’s also a good option for holiday movie nights, with classics like Home Alone and The Santa Clause.

Sources indicate that although the plan doesn’t include live sports, it supports simultaneous streaming on two devices and gives you access to everything from award-winning films like Sinners and Marty Supreme to Wuthering Heights. There’s arguably even more to watch on the TV front, from dramas like The Gilded Age, Lanterns, Euphoria, and Heated Rivalry to comedies such as Hacks and The Righteous Gemstones. Fantasy fans, meanwhile, can immerse themselves in the world of Game of Thrones and its spinoffs, including House of the Dragon and A Knight of the Seven Kingdoms, or check out Dune: Prophecy. You’ll also be able to stream new releases, including HBO’s upcoming Harry Potter series.

Recent findings suggest that paramount Plus includes CBS reveals like NCIS and Everybody Loves Raymond to Tulsa King and the various Yellowstone spinoffs, including both 1883 and 1923. Movie fans can also browse Paramount’s film library, which includes titles like Arrival, Top Gun, and Interstellar, while sports fans can watch select NFL games, UFC events, UEFA Champions League matches, and March Madness games. Premium also grants you access to Showtime originals and a live feed of your local CBS station, along with ad-free on-demand viewing, though live programming still includes commercials.

Recent findings suggest that six months should give you plenty of time to work through Apple’s other originals, including Severance, Pachinko, The Morning Show, and Pluribus, or settle in for a movie like Arrival or Anchorman. The service also includes live sports, specifically Formula 1 races and Major League Soccer matches.

All three subscriptions offer access to Crunchyroll’s full anime library without ads, including new episodes shortly after they air in Japan. The Fan tier lets you watch on one device at a time, while Mega Fan increases that limit to four devices and adds offline viewing and access to Crunchyroll’s Game Vault. Ultimate Fan, meanwhile, supports six simultaneous streams and includes Crunchyroll Manga, along with additional store perks.

Sources indicate that amazon is also discounting a wide range of subscriptions through Prime Video, including NBA League Pass, AMC Plus, MGM Plus, and several bundles. Most of the deals below are available through November 30th.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Google this weekend rolled out the latest update to Pixel Weather with a newly introduced reporting feature and small interface tweaks.

Sources indicate that on the homepage, cities that have active weather warnings no longer have bright red card backgrounds. The pill-shaped container retains its Dynamic Color theming with just the text of the warning in red. This change also extends to the card on the city page. Finally, the source, like “Google Weather,” at the very bottom is now themed.

The main change today is a “Report current weather” feature to “Share the current weather condition to improve local forecasts.” The card appears at the very bottom of your current location and can be moved up the feed.

Google claims to “Submit a report if the weather conditions don’t look right.” Tapping “Submit a report” brings up a “Report weather in [city]” sheet. You can submit two pieces of information:.

According to recent reports, on the privacy front: “Your feedback, device location and some diagnostic information will be collected to help improve forecasts. This information will not be associated with your Google account.”.

This is rolling out with version 1.1.20261012.x of Pixel Weather that widely rolled out this weekend.

MacBook Neo vs MacBook Air: Which should you buy right now?

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Apple’s Mac lineup is stronger than ever this year, largely thanks to the newly introduced MacBook Neo.
  • The MacBook Neo is Apple’s most affordable laptop ever, starting at $699 (currently on sale for $599).
  • Unlike Apple’s other Macs, the MacBook Neo is powered by an A-series chip rather than an M-series chip.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Apple’s Mac lineup is stronger than ever this year, largely thanks to the newly introduced MacBook Neo. If you’re deciding between the MacBook Neo and the MacBook Air this holiday season, here’s everything you need to know.

The MacBook Neo is Apple’s most affordable laptop ever, starting at $699 (currently on sale for $599). It features a solid aluminum design that comes in a range of fun colors, including Silver, Blush, Citrus, and Indigo.

Unlike Apple’s other Macs, the MacBook Neo is powered by an A-series chip rather than an M-series chip. It uses the A18 Pro chip originally introduced with the iPhone 16 Pro, featuring a 6-core CPU and 5-core GPU.

The MacBook Neo comes with 8GB of unified memory, with no additional RAM configuration options available. It starts with 256GB of storage, with a 512GB configuration available for an additional $100. That $100 upgrade also gets you Touch ID, which is not included in the base model.

There are some other trade-offs compared to the MacBook Air. The MacBook Neo lacks a backlit keyboard, MagSafe charging, and a Force Touch trackpad. It also has more limited USB-C connectivity and supports just one external display.

In a recent development, still, the MacBook Neo offers an impressive feature set. It has a 13-inch display, up to 16 hours of battery life, a 1080p FaceTime camera, and the full macOS experience.

It has been revealed that the MacBook Air, meanwhile, was updated earlier this year with Apple’s M5 chip. It starts at $1,299, making it $600 more expensive than the entry-level MacBook Air. The MacBook Air is currently on sale with a starting price of $999.

For that $600 upgrade, the MacBook Air offers several key advantages over the MacBook Air. The M5 chip has a 10-core CPU and up to a 10-core GPU, enabling better sustained performance than the MacBook Neo.

The MacBook Air also starts with 16GB of unified memory and 512GB of storage, both double the entry-level MacBook Neo. You can configure it with up to 32GB of memory and 4TB of storage, while the MacBook Neo is limited to 8GB of memory and 512GB of storage.

Apple rates the MacBook Air for up to 18 hours of video streaming and 15 hours of wireless web browsing, compared to 16 hours and 11 hours, respectively, for the MacBook Neo.

As I wrote in my review earlier this year, I think the MacBook Neo is a great Mac, full stop … not just because of the great price. It can handle the vast majority of things most people will throw at it. This includes web browsing, basic photo and video editing, research, and much more.

The M5 MacBook Air, meanwhile, offers more power and more configuration options. This makes it a great option for people who need more storage, RAM, and power than the MacBook Neo can offer.

According to recent reports, one of my favorite things about the MacBook Air is that it’s available in two screen sizes. The 15-inch MacBook Air is one of my favorite Apple laptops with a combination of the ultra-thin and light design and the larger screen. I think a lot of people forget it exists, but it’s an excellent choice.

To recap, I think the MacBook Neo is a great choice for everyday tasks like web browsing, email, writing, and streaming. The MacBook Air is a better fit for more demanding workflows, including photo and video editing, coding, working with large spreadsheets, and heavy multitasking.

Beyond performance, the MacBook Air offers a handful of niceties that you won’t find on the MacBook Neo. These include a backlit keyboard, a larger display with True Tone, MagSafe charging, a better webcam and speakers, and a Force Touch trackpad. It also includes Touch ID on every configuration, longer battery life, and support for two external displays.

If it’s in the budget, I think the MacBook Air is an excellent choice for all Mac shoppers. It’s plenty powerful, thin and light, and is highly configurable compared to the MacBook Neo.

What do you think of the MacBook Neo vs MacBook Air decision? Which would you choose? Let us know down in the comments.

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • The judge has preliminarily sided with ABC, rejecting the FCC’s efforts to dismiss the case.﻿.
  • The judge has preliminarily sided with ABC, rejecting the FCC’s efforts to dismiss the case.﻿.
  • Sources indicate that US District Judge Loren AliKhan has blocked the Federal Communications Commission from conducting an early review of ABC’s broadcast licenses in a preliminary injunction, and rejected its efforts to dismiss ABC’s First Amendment lawsuit.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The judge has preliminarily sided with ABC, rejecting the FCC’s efforts to dismiss the case.﻿.

The judge has preliminarily sided with ABC, rejecting the FCC’s efforts to dismiss the case.﻿.

Sources indicate that US District Judge Loren AliKhan has blocked the Federal Communications Commission from conducting an early review of ABC’s broadcast licenses in a preliminary injunction, and rejected its efforts to dismiss ABC’s First Amendment lawsuit. ABC has accused the FCC of violating its free speech rights and claims the agency “waged a retaliatory campaign” against the network over content it broadcast. In her ruling the judge noted that the network was “likely to succeed on their retaliation claim.”.

According to recent reports, although Disney, ABC’s parent organization, wasn’t set to renew its broadcast licenses until 2028, last April the FCC ordered the network to file for an early license renewal claiming it was part of an investigation into Disney’s policies on diversity, equity, and inclusivity. The FCC’s move came a day after President Donald Trump demanded ABC fire late-night talk show host Jimmy Kimmel following a skit about Melania Trump.

Recent findings suggest that in response to the FCC’s order, Disney and ABC sued the agency in August and accused the FCC of “punishing ABC for its speech” by threatening its broadcast licenses. The preliminary injunction issued by the judge on Wednesday prohibits the FCC from taking any further action in the early review of ABC’s broadcast licenses and noted that the network had shown that the court’s intervention in the agency’s actions was in the public interest.

Recent findings suggest that ”No one doubts that the Commission may enforce the law in the manner it sees fit,” the judge wrote. “But in doing so, Defendants may not retaliate against or punish Plaintiffs and other broadcast license holders for disfavored speech.”.

When I'm in a rush to leave the house, there's only one pair of earbuds that I shove into my pocket without a second thought: the Beats Solo Buds.

They're extremely compact and lightweight thanks to a sophisticated design that ditches the usual clunky earpod case battery and instead crams 18 hours of juice into each bud on a single charge, so they're easy to take on the go.

Industry observers note that better still, their Fast Fuel quick-charging feature means that you can squeeze an hour of playback out of a single hour of charge – and this is something I rely on all the time. I plug the buds directly into my phone's charging port when they're dead for a quick charge when I need a bit of extra juice. It's a real lifesaver and means that, as long as I carry a small cable, I never have to worry about being without my tunes.

Sources indicate that at just £39 (was £79), thanks to a mega EE discount, they're also simply incredible value and pack in plenty of that trademark Beats sound despite the small form factor. Beats may be owned by Apple, but that doesn't mean the Solo Buds don't play nice with Android. They support Google Fast Pair, and even have an Android companion app. (If you are an Apple user, they work perfectly with that ecosystem, too.).

These compact earbuds are a steal at under £40. They come in a wide range of attractive colors (though the translucent red is my personal favorite) and are both practical and stylish. EE is even throwing in free delivery.

✅Recommended if: You're after a seriously compact pair of earbuds that you won't need to worry about keeping charged.

According to recent reports, the Beats Solo Buds are some of the smallest and lightest wireless earbuds I've ever used when in their case, making them easy to take on the go. The Fast Fuel feature also makes them very quick to top up with charge, even when you're out and about.

Recent findings suggest that ❌Skip this deal if: You want to spend more and get better sound. Although I think the Beats Solo Buds can hold their own in the under £100 audio space with their poppy and bassy sound, the brand doesn't exactly have a reputation for audiophile quality.

If you want to spend more on something that sounds even better, you have plenty of options to choose from in the ongoing sales.

The countdown to Black Friday is on, and many discounts have already arrived. Although the shopping holiday isn’t officially until tomorrow, November 27th, retailers are already dropping early deals on some of our favorite tech. Of course, with prices rising across the board, a good discount doesn’t necessarily mean you’re getting a historically low price. But we’re still seeing worthwhile discounts on a wide variety of tried-and-tested gear, with more expected later this weekend.

Recent findings suggest that below, we’ve rounded up the best early Black Friday deals we’ve found so far. Prices could drop further as Black Friday approaches, as is always the case, but these deals are worth considering if you’d rather shop early and beat the holiday rush. We’ll continue to enhancement this guide as more retailers launch their holiday sales, too, so be sure to check back regularly as we get closer to the main event.

According to recent reports, apple’s AirPods Pro 3 deliver the best noise cancellation and sound quality of any AirPods yet, along with a more comfortable, secure fit and improved water resistance. They also feature built-in heart rate tracking for workouts and support live translations for a handful of languages. Read our review.

You can get an ad-supported Disney Plus and Hulu bundle for $4.99 a month ($8 off) for an entire year. Both streaming services feature a deep catalog of new and classic TV highlights and movies, including The Simpsons, Andor, Toy Story 5, and The Fantastic Four: First Steps.

Apple’s latest AirTags feature an upgraded ultra-wideband chip for more precise location tracking, a noticeably louder speaker, and an expanded Bluetooth range. Read our review.

Android app developers will soon have to share their address publicly

📅 26 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (369 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: The Verge

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • The change is to meet EU regulations, but Apple gives its developers more privacy.﻿.
  • The change is to meet EU regulations, but Apple gives its developers more privacy.﻿.
  • Independent Android app developers are worried about their privacy after Google revealed that from next year many of them will be required to share a phone number and address publicly.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The change is to meet EU regulations, but Apple gives its developers more privacy.﻿.

The change is to meet EU regulations, but Apple gives its developers more privacy.﻿.

Independent Android app developers are worried about their privacy after Google revealed that from next year many of them will be required to share a phone number and address publicly. The policy change is intended to meet European Union regulations under the Digital Services Act, but Google says contact details will be made public worldwide.

Developers have until February 1st 2027 to declare whether or not they’re a “trader” under UK and European law. Broadly speaking, Google indicates the definition applies if you earn revenue from your apps, especially if that revenue is regular or at high volume. Developers are exempt if their apps are only a hobby or non-commercial, or if they simply don’t publish them in the UK or Europe.

Industry observers note that if they self-declare as a trader, developers’ contact details will be shared publicly starting March 1st, including a phone number and address. Google doesn’t accept PO boxes for developer payment profile addresses, meaning many independent developers without an office will either have to share their home address online or pay for a registered agent or other service that provides a business address. One independent developer told The Elec they were considering renting a private office solely to comply with the new rules. We’ve asked Google to confirm why developers aren’t permitted to publish a PO box address, and why details are being shared globally, and will revision this article when we hear back.

Sources indicate that apple is subject to the same regulations, but is handling them differently to Google. It will only display developer addresses within the relevant European countries, rather than publishing them worldwide. It’s also allowing developers to supply PO box addresses, so long as they provide Apple with a receipt or bill that links the PO box to their regular address.

Update, November 26th: Added mention of developers’ option to use a registered agent service for a business address.

The iOS notifications system is overdue for an update. While Apple has added features like Apple Intelligence-based priority notifications and notification summaries, the system still lacks other organization and sorting settings.

I’d love for Apple to adopt a similar system on iPhone, iPad, and Mac. Even with the recent Apple Intelligence additions, the iOS notifications system is still far too basic.

On the hunt for substantial Black Friday 2026 savings on this type of gear? Our team of experts has been tracking the best offers from the sales event so far — click through to find out more.

Smart video doorbells used to be quite expensive, but unlike smartphones, which have gotten considerably more expensive over the past year, video doorbells seem to have gone in the opposite direction. You can get a pretty good one for surprisingly little money these days, with even some of the cheaper models offering features like 2K video recording, night vision, and two-way audio.

Recent findings suggest that and thanks to the ongoing Black Friday sale, they've gotten even cheaper. In fact, some of the biggest names in the smart home space, including Ring, Arlo, and Blink, are offering discounts of over 50% on their video doorbells right now. I've rounded up five deals worth checking out, including a couple of options that don't require a monthly subscription to save your recordings.

What's even better is that four of them cost less than $40/.

Sources indicate that if you're looking for an affordable way to get started with smart home security, it's hard to argue with this $22 Blink video doorbell. It offers 2K video quality with a head-to-toe view, night vision, and noise cancellation for clearer conversations. Since it's a wired doorbell, you don't have to worry about recharging it either. You'll need a compatible Alexa device or a separately sold Blink Chime for in-home doorbell alerts, though.

If you'd rather get a wireless video doorbell, Arlo's second-generation model is available for just $28. It offers 2K HDR video, two-way audio, and night vision, so you can see and speak to whoever's at your front door even at night. There's also support for person and package detection, though you'll need an Arlo Secure subscription to access those advanced features.

Sources indicate that at just $38, the Tapo D205 is a great option if you don't want to pay for a subscription or a separate storage hub. It supports local recording via a microSD card of up to 512GB and offers AI-powered person detection at no extra cost. You also get a 2K camera with a 160-degree field of view, night vision, two-way audio, and a built-in 5,200 mAh battery for up to 180 days of use.

It has been revealed that if you already have a couple of Amazon Echo devices around your house, this Ring video doorbell is probably the one I'd recommend. It features video with up to 6x zoom, two-way audio, and motion alerts. You can also receive doorbell notifications through your Echo speakers or pull up the live camera feed on an Echo Show.

It has been revealed that the Eufy E340 is a little more expensive than the other video doorbells on this list, but it comes with two cameras: one to see who's at your front door and another to keep an eye on your packages. You also get 2K video and 8GB of built-in local storage without a monthly subscription. Plus, you can use it as either a wired or battery-powered doorbell.

Personally, I'd spend a little extra on a video doorbell that supports local storage. It's nice being able to go back and check what happened outside your house without having to pay for yet another monthly subscription.

Industry observers note that the Tapo D205 is particularly appealing in that regard at just $38. That noted, if you regularly get packages delivered to your doorstep, the dual-camera setup on the Eufy E340 might be worth the extra money.
