It has been revealed that this isn't to say that U.S. agencies didn't find any link between Ms. Huang and the Chinese government at all. U.S. officials reportedly stated that China's Ministry of State Security asked Ms. Huang to provide them with some unspecified information, which she allegedly did in accordance with Chinese law. They also claimed that her husband, businessman Kang Wei, was a Chinese intelligence asset. However, while the full extent of Ms. Huang's relationship with the Chinese government remains unclear, there is reportedly nothing to suggest that she passed on any significant information.

The Chinese government has consistently rejected claims that Ms. Huang was an intelligence agent. In an Oct. 30 press conference, Chinese Ministry of Foreign Affairs spokesperson Guo Jiakun called such reports "unsubstantiated" and "nothing but smears against China." He later reiterated China's stance after Huang revealed his first affair on Nov. 8.

"On the so-called 'Chinese spy,' we have made our position clear," Chinese Ministry of Foreign Affairs spokesperson Mao Ning remarked in a Nov. 12 press briefing. "China's sci-tech progress relies on independent innovation and open cooperation. The U.S. should stop fabricating the 'Chinese spy' narratives as a pretext for imposing technology restrictions.".

It has been revealed that the U.S. government at the moment restricts Nvidia's chip sales to China, citing national security concerns. Several other categories of foreign-made devices are also banned from entering the U.S. due to national security, including WiFi routers and robot vacuums.

In a recent development, in 1993, Nvidia co-founders Huang, Chris Malachowsky, and Curtis Priem met in the San Jose Denny's to discuss ideas for the chip that would lead them to launch their firm. Ten years later, Denny's erected a commemorative plaque in the booth they'd used.

Industry observers note that "The booth that released a $1 trillion company," the plaque read at the time. Nvidia's value has since climbed to over $4 trillion, though recent turmoil has caused significant fluctuation. "Congratulations, Nvidia! Who knew that an idea started here would change the world?" Ever had something to say, but later? WhatsApp now lets you schedule messages that will be automatically sent at a designated time.

You can line up messages to be delivered anytime from 10 minutes to 14 days later, either to your one-on-one or group chats. Scheduled messages can have text, photos, and videos.

The feature has been one of the most requested features on WhatsApp, the tech giant stated in a blog post.

The Apple iPhone 18 Pro is free right now with T-Mobile.

In a recent development, to schedule a message in WhatsApp, press and hold the send button, then pick the time and date for the message to arrive. Key: The receiving party won't know that it's a scheduled message, and they'll be delighted that you remembered their birthday even though you merely used an AI agent to schedule everyone's birthday messages automatically (we kid, we would never).

Just like normal messages, the scheduled messages will be end-to-end encrypted. Also, WhatsApp points out that they'll be sent even if your phone is off or out of battery.

According to WhatsApp, scheduled messages are rolling out globally "over the coming weeks.".

First and foremost, the parade starts at 8:30 a.m. ET and runs until noon on Saturday. Yes, you read that right: The Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade is not actually on Thanksgiving Day this year. There are very good reasons for that, which we'll get to in a second.

Industry observers note that it's worth noting that, unlike most other live televised events, it will not air simultaneously in every time zone. Instead, per NBC News, it will air from 8:30 to around noon in each time zone, so no matter where you are, turn the TV on at 8:30.

The parade will air on NBC, so if you have a TV that gets local channels via cable, an antenna, or another way to watch TV, just turn on NBC.

How Hinges deep-learning Most Compatible feature actually works, and how to train it

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Ever since its introduction in 2018, Hinge's "Most Compatible" feature has earned equal parts praise and scorn from online daters, who can't seem to decide if it's the best thing ever or a bad joke.
  • Even today, eight years after it was first introduced, Most Compatible is a marvel of mathematical engineering, beginning with its foundation: the Gale-Shapley algorithm (also known as the propose-and-reject algorithm), developed all the way back in 1962 to solve a (hypothetical) mating problem.
  • Recent findings suggest that hinge's variation of the algorithm works dynamically, constantly taking into account user preferences and choices to predict what kind of person you would most like to date.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Ever since its introduction in 2018, Hinge's "Most Compatible" feature has earned equal parts praise and scorn from online daters, who can't seem to decide if it's the best thing ever or a bad joke.

Even today, eight years after it was first introduced, Most Compatible is a marvel of mathematical engineering, beginning with its foundation: the Gale-Shapley algorithm (also known as the propose-and-reject algorithm), developed all the way back in 1962 to solve a (hypothetical) mating problem.

Recent findings suggest that hinge's variation of the algorithm works dynamically, constantly taking into account user preferences and choices to predict what kind of person you would most like to date. At the start of each upcoming day, you will receive a Most Compatible profile suggestion that expires after 24 hours unless you interact with it.

AdultFriendFinder — readers’ pick for casual connections.

Tinder — top pick for fast hookups.

Hinge — popular choice for regular meetups.

Pure — best for anonymous hookups.

OkCupid — best app for inclusivity.

But there's a massive catch here that too many Hinge users are unaware of: your own actions and inactions are factored into the equation, so if you feed the algorithm bad data, it won't work in your favor, and you'll rarely see a compelling profile suggestion. We reached out to Hinge to gain a better understanding of their algorithm from the inside, and they described it as a "recommendation system" that combines multiple algorithms, "using your stated preferences and your activity on the app," to adjust and refine its suggestions.

Here are three key tips from Hinge to help its recommendation algorithm work for you:.

Too many Hinge people (and men in particular!) cast a wide net, interacting with as many profiles as possible, sending out Likes all over the place. We get it: the more-is-more approach has its appeal, but it actually hurts the algorithm's effectiveness, since it becomes harder to narrow down your preferences when you're too indiscriminate about who you like or interact with.

Or, as Hinge told us: "If you send too many likes, we can’t tell what you truly want. At the same time, if you rarely send likes, we don’t have enough information to learn from about who excites you. By engaging with others with curiosity and purpose, your recommendations meaningfully evolve alongside you.".

Recent findings suggest that instead of being overly enthusiastic in your search, be intentional: take your time to vet profiles and interact only with people you can genuinely see yourself dating. You may not even necessarily know what these profiles might have in common, but rest assured the algorithm will be at work in the background finding the common thread and refining its suggestions for you in the future.

Sources indicate that the default Hinge filters are very relaxed, but there's actually a Dealbreakers toggle hidden in the Dating Preferences section of your profile. The normal preferences (location and age range, for example) are taken into account but treated more like guidelines than hard limits. However, if you start enabling your Dealbreakers, Hinge will treat them as hard limits and never even show you profiles that don't match your preferences. As Hinge put it to us, "Hinge will only show you each other if you both meet the dealbreakers that either of you set, such as wanting kids. This helps you focus on people who feel like a real long-term match.".

Industry observers note that most dating app consumers, out of sheer eagerness to start browsing local singles, make a half-hearted attempt to fill out their profiles, usually doing the bare minimum to meet the app's requirements. But Hinge offers an extremely generous array of profile fields, and the more you fill out, the more data the algorithm can use to do its matchmaking work.

And as Hinge pointed out to us, not answering a question is treated like a negative, actively shrinking your dating pool: "When you select 'prefer not to say,' it limits who can see you. From family plans and dating intentions to drinking habits, you're excluded from being shown to people who've set Dealbreakers around those compatibility factors.".

We recommend you put particular focus on filling out Hinge's prompts in a thoughtful way, taking particular care to choose ones that reflect directly on your personality or interests.

In Hinge's own profile guide, they offer vital advice that is too often overlooked: ditch the clichés and one-word or low-effort responses, and take the time to give a personal answer to every question. And take the time to answer a voice prompt, as you'll be rewarded by the algorithm for doing so.

Finally, there's good evidence that Hinge's algorithm rewards profiles with refreshed photos, so if you haven't updated your main photos in a minute, follow their photo refresh guide to optimize your new pics.

If you follow the steps above, you should start to see the algorithm working more in your favor, and you'll look forward to each day's latest Most Compatible suggestion.

But that's still not all. Lopez also cracks jokes about her many marriages with an uncrackable face, and generally mythologizes herself through selected anecdotes. And that is still not all.

Performing numbers reminiscent of West Side Story and Chicago, JLo also lets Broadway know what they're missing. Much like her wild autobiographical visual album This is Me...Now, The JLo Show offers Lopez doing too much, and being absolutely dazzling all the while. — K.P.

How to watch: The JLo Show debuts on Paramount+ on Nov. 26.

Remember how Curtis "50 Cent" Jackson produced a doc about Diddy that made the public reconsider the 1996 murder of Tupac Shakur (among other things)? Well, if you binge-watched Netflix's Sean Combs: The Reckoning, we wager you're already seated for The Tupac Tapes with Angie Martinez.

Recent findings suggest that this one focuses on Radio Hall of Famer and New York Times bestselling author Angie Martinez, as she looks back on her taped interview with Shakur, recorded in his Los Angeles home months before his death. In this four-part video podcast, Martinez plays portions of the tapes never heard before by the public. Plus, she discusses Shakur's life, legacy, and death with guests like Charlamagne Tha God, Joe Budden, Big Boy, Dream Hampton, RZA, and Wallo. — K.P.

How to watch: The Tupac Tapes with Angie Martinez debuts on Netflix on Nov. 27.

In a recent development, it can be hard to get scientific research funded. And in writer-director Alex Goyette's horror Breeder, no one knows this better than MIT dropout Russell (Daniel Doheny). But it seems like his luck has changed when he finds an investor in Patti Kolb (Glee's Dot-Marie Jones), an affluent breeder of minature poodles. There's just one catch. She wants to meet him. In person. At her remote ranch. Where she's got a fleet of young women in residence.

As you might guess from this setup (or the trailer above), Kolb isn't only interested in breeding dogs. And her methods for studs that don't meet her expectations are...harsh. It's little wonder that this mean indie has been gathering praise all summer long as it hit the film festival circus. Now you can see what horror lovers have been barking about. — K.P.

Starring: Daniel Doheny, Dot-Marie Jones, Maddie Phillips, and Tanaya Beatty.

How to watch: Breeder is now available on digital.

Romanian filmmaker Cristian Mungiu was previously best known for his 2007 drama 4 Months, 3 Weeks and 2 Days. However, after winning the Palme d'Or at this year's Cannes Film Festival for Fjord, he's finding a latest international audience, with a little help from the MCU's Sebastian Stan.

Recent findings suggest that with a shaved head and bushy beard, Stan is unrecognizable from his role as the Winter Soldier. Opposite Norwegian film star Renate Reinsve (The Worst Person in the World, Sentimental Value), he plays a soft-spoken Romanian engineer, who's moved his wife and children to Norway to be closer to her family. But cultural differences hit hard, as the family's evangelical Christian devotion is seen as suffocating and even abusive by the children's teachers. When child protective services step in, Fjord becomes part family-drama, part crime-drama, inviting audiences to make their own decisions about right and wrong. — K.P.

Starring: Sebastian Stan and Renate Reinsve.

How to watch: Fjord is now available on digital.

Aside from holding titles from the World Boxing Council and the International Boxing Organization, British boxer Tyson Fury might be best known for his ferocity and endurance in the ring. However, his Netflix documentary, Tyson Fury, goes behind his tough exterior to reveal his tenderness.

Interviews with his fighter father John Fury reveal a trying childhood, as well as the shocking revelation that challenged Tyson's idea of his dad. Director Lucy Wilcox also interviews his wife, Paris Fury, who gives insights into the boxer as a supportive partner and loving father. Wilcox's approach to Tyson is compassionate, giving him space to be vulnerable as he talks about his trauma, his self-esteem concerns, and his struggles with suicidal ideation. And yet, she doesn't avoid touchy topics, like the public backlash over his comments about homosexuality and women. So, while this is an empathetic portrait of the fighter, it's also as hard-hitting as its subject. — K.P.

Starring: Tyson Fury, Paris Fury, and John Fury.

Industry observers note that how to watch: Tyson Fury debuts on Netflix on Nov. 27.

If you haven't had an entanglement with Wicker in regular unmoving cinemas or in rumbling 4DX, this is your chance to log it. Based on Ursula Wills-Jones' short story "The Wicker Husband," this raunchy, hilarious, heartwarming fairy tale sees a fisherwoman (Olivia Colman) requesting a basket weaver (Peter Dinklage) to literally make her a husband in order to spite the local townspeople (led by Elizabeth Debicki). And it works, with Alexander Skarsgård brought to life as a dashing wicker man.

"It's a deeply silly, fairy tale concept," I wrote in my review. "But what directors Alex Huston Fischer and Eleanor Wilson have up their sleeve is a hilarious and heartfelt script, an incredibly talented cast, and magical production design...It's an artisanal Frankenstein tale, and one that will melt that brittle basket-woven heart of yours — or simply have you thinking about Taylor Swift's "Wood" differently." — S.C.

Starring: Olivia Colman, Alexander Skarsgård, Peter Dinklage, and Elizabeth Debicki.

How to watch: Wicker is now available on digital.

Amy Poehler reunites with Parks and Recreation co-creator Mike Schur for Dig, a charming sitcom based on Kate Myers's novel Excavations. Poehler plays Elise, lead archaeologist on a Grecian archaeological dig. When she makes the discovery of a lifetime, she'll team up with a crew of fellow passionate archaeologists to uncover it in secret, far from the prying eyes of egotistical dig head Neville (Hugh Laurie).

While not always laugh-out-loud funny, Dig is a perfect warm and cozy watch, not to mention a wonderful character study of its wonderful core ensemble, made up of Poehler, Laurie, Geraldine Viswanathan, Antonia Thomas, and Fina Strazza. As I wrote in my review, "despite the flashy location and a latest mystery twist, Dig retains the core formula that made Parks and Recreation so irresistible: investing deeply in a lovable new crew of unlikely friends." — B.E.

Starring: Amy Poehler, Hugh Laurie, Geraldine Viswanathan, Antonia Thomas, and Fina Strazza.

How to watch: Dig premieres Nov. 23 on Peacock, with new episodes on Mondays.

You've never seen Blade Runner like you will in Blade Runner 2099. The TV series upends the hierarchy of the prior Blade Runner films entirely. Following a brutal uprising, replicants are now in control of humanity. Now, replicant blade runners are in charge of hunting rogue humans — among these is Cora (Hunter Schafer). Tired of running, she undertakes a dangerous mission that forces her to pose as a blade runner. She'll soon cross paths with blade runner Olwen (Michelle Yeoh), a replicant with only days left to live. In those final days, she and Cora will search for a group of runaway replicants on the hunt for a secret that can change the world.

Industry observers note that yeoh and Schafer are a match made in heaven, each handling Blade Runner 2099's action with eternal cool. Their unofficial third co-star is the world around them, brought to brilliant life by the production team. Imposing pyramids and seedy shops shine under neon lighting and threatening dust clouds, while Vangelis-esque synths usher us into a sense of cyberpunk noir. It's a towering technical achievement fronted by two exceptional leads, and a worthy addition to the Blade Runner franchise. — B.E.

Starring: Michelle Yeoh, Hunter Schafer, Dimitri Abold, Lewis Gribben, Katelyn Rose Downey, Daniel Rigby, Johnny Harris, Amy Lennox, Sheila Atim, Matthew Needham, Tom Burke, and Maurizio Lombardi.

Sources indicate that how to watch: Blade Runner 2099 premieres Nov. 25 on Prime Video.

Arguably the most talked-about movie of the year has landed on digital. And you better believe that's going to mean a fresh round of memes, spoofs, debates, and obsession.

Canadian comedian Nathan Fielder — of all people — interviewing notorious Theranos founder Elizabeth Holmes in her home, ahead of her prison sentence? How could that be a real movie? It's buzz has even reached space.

Recent findings suggest that we're still saying the best way to see You Can See Everything is in theaters. But we're also giddy at the chance to be able to pause, rewind, and geek out with friends on a whole upcoming level now that we have the remote. — K.P.

Starring: Nathan Fielder, Elizabeth Holmes, and Billy Evans.

How to watch: You Can See Everything is available for purchase on Prime Video.

#3171. Apple Watch Series 12 review: Same design, better health tracking, and more listening in

📅 26 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 8m • 📚 Deep Dive (1586 w)
📖 Baca
Gadgets ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Mashable ↗ Open Full Page

Apple Watch Series 12 review: Same design, better health tracking, and more listening in

📅 26 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1586 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Mashable

⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Looks are deceiving for the upcoming Apple Watch Series 12.
  • After wearing the Series 12 for the past three-ish weeks, I'm pleased to report that some of these invisible upgrades make a pretty meaningful difference — and that they don't chip away at the watch's battery life.
  • According to recent reports, that remarked, I wouldn't miss half of the new AI-powered "Audio Intelligence" tools if Apple suddenly Thanos-snapped them out of existence.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Looks are deceiving for the upcoming Apple Watch Series 12. On the outside, it appears to be the exact same smartwatch as last year (...and the year before that). But on the inside, it packs redesigned heart rate sensors and a faster S11 chip that enables intriguing new health-tracking features and AI tools, including the Siri AI beta.

After wearing the Series 12 for the past three-ish weeks, I'm pleased to report that some of these invisible upgrades make a pretty meaningful difference — and that they don't chip away at the watch's battery life. My testing found that the Series 12 lasts slightly longer than the Series 11 from fall 2025.

According to recent reports, that remarked, I wouldn't miss half of the new AI-powered "Audio Intelligence" tools if Apple suddenly Thanos-snapped them out of existence. Always-on AI notetakers like Plaud, Pocket, and Bee are a growing trend in Silicon Valley, but they're not for me.

The Series 12's external changes are primarily cosmetic. Apple added a ceramic case option to the mix again, giving buyers a fresh premium alternative to its aluminum and titanium variants (which now come in new shades like dark bronze and radiant gold). There are some fresh band styles and materials to chew over, too. For testing, Apple sent me a Series 12 with a light gold aluminum case and a sand Sport Band. I'm more of a silver girl myself, but it's very pretty.

Industry observers note that each case type is available in 42mm or 46mm sizes, as usual. They're priced as follows:.

Aluminum case: Starting at $399 with optional cellular connectivity ($100 extra).

Titanium case: Starting at $699 with cellular connectivity.

Ceramic case: Starting at $899 with cellular connectivity.

Industry observers note that all of the Series 12's case options are still waterproof for up to 50 meters and carry an IP6X dust resistance rating, but Apple indicates the glass on the aluminum Series 12 is more durable than before. Otherwise, it's identical to the Series 11 (which was basically identical to the Series 10).

Sources indicate that longtime Apple Watch users who are holding out for an exciting redesign might just stop reading here, understandably. If it's any consolation, we might get one next year. But as someone fresh to the wearable space, I will say this is a very attractive and comfortable watch. Familiarity breeds contempt, as St. Augustine or Taylor Swift or whomever once said.

Industry observers note that located on the underside of its base, the Series 12's fresh "Health Sensing System" is a cluster of advanced optical and electrical heart sensors. It has more electrodes that cover a larger surface area for better skin contact during ECG readings, rearranged photodiodes that are better at picking up light, and bigger, more efficient green LEDs that take readings way more frequently.

While older Apple Watches only logged the user's heart rate continuously during workouts and every five minutes otherwise, the Series 12 now measures heart rate every five seconds throughout the day, no matter what you're doing. As proof, these near-real-time readings are available at a glance on a new heart rate watch face widget, or "complication.".

According to recent reports, the Series 12's fancier sensors also up the frequency of its heart rate variability readings from every two hours to every five minutes. (HRV is a key stress indicator.).

These changes make the Series 12's heart rate data much more precise and detailed than before, and more useful for non-athletes. In turn, other features that use this data should be more accurate, too — Vitals and the Exercise ring, to name a couple. I think this will be the Series 12's biggest selling point for most people.

In a recent development, apple reworked its pedometer model for the Series 12 to track steps more accurately when your arms are still. It also added a step count complication, aptly called "Steps." That one might not seem like a huge deal, but it actually resolves a common pain point with older Apple Watches: Customers previously had to DIY a step-count complication by installing a separate pedometer app. It's great to see.

Industry observers note that the Series 12 can now produce a "Readiness" score, a 0 to 10 rating of your capacity for physical activity based on your recent exercise, sleep habits, and Vitals. It needs a week of data before it starts working, FYI. The best tech deal this week The Apple iPhone 18 Pro is free right now with T-Mobile.

The Apple iPhone 18 Pro is free right now with T-Mobile.

I like that this score adjusts throughout the day — it's not a one-and-done daily reading. One of my mornings started at a 6 ("Ready") after a decent night's sleep. By the evening that same day, it had fallen to a 4 ("Pace Yourself") because I went on a long, brisk afternoon walk.

That noted, the feature mostly tells me what I could already figure out on my own. I don't necessarily need a score to know I'm less inclined to work out right after exercising. Athletes with more varied training regimens will probably get more value out of this feature than the average person.

The Series 12's four Audio Intelligence features use its built-in microphone to pick up on sounds and conversations. To address privacy concerns, Apple claims it has ensured it doesn't create or store any recordings and that the raw audio is completely inaccessible before it's deleted. And if you're really weirded out by them, you can just opt out.

Music Recognition with Shazam now works automatically. It usually takes only a couple of seconds to identify a song, depending on the amount of background noise, and it's always spot-on.

Sound Recognition can alert you to sounds such as sirens, doorbells, smoke alarms, barking dogs, and car horns. It liked to confuse a train's "door closing" chime for an appliance bell, but was otherwise accurate in my testing. It's a useful addition for people who are deaf and hard of hearing.

It has been revealed that live Rewind transcribes the tail end of a recent conversation when you double-press the Series 12's dial (aka "Digital Crown"). Apple notes it can show the last 15 seconds of speech, but in practice it's closer to 10 seconds. Either way, it feels kind of pointless. It's such a short window of time that you might as well just ask the person you're chatting with to repeat themselves. It's also not correct 100 percent of the time. It once confused the phrase "pencil me in" for "Pennsylvania.".

Finally, there's Siri Recap, which is essentially a built-in AI notetaker. (It's meant for oral conversations, but it's also summarized TikToks I've watched and phone calls I've taken on speaker mode.) Its outlines are pretty macro and vary in their helpfulness depending on the conversation. I found it really good for recapping food orders and reviewing topics discussed in my Italian classes, but a little clunky when it comes to casual conversations. It doesn't distinguish between different speakers and sometimes mashes topics together. It's also not completely accurate — it noted a friend named their baby "Popsicle" (no <3) — but it seems to be improving as I've continued to use it.

Recent findings suggest that I struggle with Siri Recap the most because it makes me feel like a creep. It doesn't alert you when it's listening in on a conversation, much less the person(s) you're speaking with, so it's on you to tell them that you're documenting your private discussions for later reference. (Awkward!) Keep in mind that such admissions will likely change the nature of your interactions: People edit themselves and put up their guards when they know they're being watched.

In a recent development, apple rated the Series 12 for up to 24 hours of battery life, but in my testing, it's offered around 45 to 51 hours of normal use per charge. (Crucially, I haven't needed to activate Low Power Mode to hit those numbers.) This is a real testament to the S11 chip's power efficiency. It's also a nice bump from the Series 11, which Mashable's Stan Schroeder described as "a one-and-a-half-day smartwatch.".

According to recent reports, apple says the Series 12 charges faster than its predecessor, too. I don't have a Series 11 handy to verify that, but I've been impressed with the Series 12's charging speed. Right before going to bed one night, I realized it didn't have enough charge for sleep tracking, which requires at least 30 percent battery. Luckily, just five minutes on an outlet bumped it from 23 to 39 percent battery.

With its latest mainstream smartwatch, Apple refines a familiar design with near-live heart rate tracking, noticeable battery-life gains, and a step-tracking widget — a small but welcome quality-of-life tweak. Audio Intelligence, meanwhile, takes a back seat to these more meaningful improvements.

In a recent development, for most people, the Series 12 is the best Apple Watch to buy right now (unless, of course, you're willing to wait for next year's redesign). It's an easy recommendation over the more expensive Apple Watch Ultra 4, which offers much of the same functionality but adds longer battery life and enhanced durability for outdoor and endurance activities. Compared to the budget-friendly Apple Watch SE 3, the Series 12 is also a more future-proof choice, with a considerably more comprehensive suite of health and fitness tracking features to boot.

Topics Apple Apple Watch Smartwatches.

Recent findings suggest that the Home Depot's BOGO Black Friday tool deal was a hit with Mashable readers last holiday season, so I'm pleased to report that it's back again. Just add certain on-sale cordless tools and kits to your cart to earn another free cordless tool worth up to $249. You can take your pick from impact drivers, saws, hammer drills, sanders, and more from popular brands like DeWalt, Makita, Milwaukee, Ridgid, and Ryobi.

Recent findings suggest that most of the best Black Friday deals are available online, so retailers have to pull out the stops to get people into their stores. And Lowe's is going hard with its free Black Friday Bucket giveaway for the second year in a row.

In a recent development, here's how it works: The first 50 MyLowe’s Rewards members in line at every store will receive a bucket containing at least 10 free products and offers. Four of those 50 buckets will include a red, green, gold, or silver ticket that earns their possessor a grand prize: either a free $2,000 major appliance, an EGO outdoor power tool, a Craftsman tools package, or a Blackstone grilling package. If you can't show up right away, fret not: The next 100 people in line will get a miniature bucket containing $5 in MyLowe’s Money and other rewards.

Industry observers note that bass Pro Shops and Cabela’s — The first 250 customers (ages 16 and older) at every store will receive a free mystery gift card worth $10 to $500, which will be valid from Dec. 6 to 24.

JCPenney — Select stores are giving away four prizes throughout the day, including a miniature Harry Potter snow globe, a Ninja air fryer, diamond earrings, and a Samsonite suitcase.

It has been revealed that michaels — Every store is giving away 500 "Countdown to Craftsmas" advent calendars. One calendar in every store contains a $100 gift card, and one recipient will win a $10,000 grand prize.

Sephora at Kohl's — The first 200 customers at select stores will receive a free Kohl’s Cash voucher worth $5 to $100 to spend on beauty purchases that day.

Recent findings suggest that target — The first 100 customers at every store will receive a free Target gift card worth $25, $50, or $100. One person per store will get a $1,000 gift card.

Industry observers note that paying for a membership just to shop a sale feels a little counterproductive. Luckily, eligible customers can try Amazon Prime free for 30 days. Starting your trial now gives you time to shop early deals and still have it for Black Friday and Cyber Monday. After the trial, Prime costs $14.99 per month or $139 per year, depending on your selected initiative.

In a recent development, prime comes with more than free shipping, though that’s probably the perk you’ll use most while shopping for gifts. You also get Prime Video, Amazon Music’s ad-free listening options, access to a selection of books through Prime Reading, and member-exclusive deals. The newest addition is $0 delivery fees on eligible Uber Eats restaurant orders of $25 or more placed through Amazon — a useful extra for the nights you’d rather order dinner than make it.

Books are one of those things I don’t particularly enjoy putting a spending limit on. A subscription at least gives you a way to read more without paying for every title separately. Kindle+, formerly Kindle Unlimited, offers a 30-day free trial with access to a catalog of ebooks, audiobooks, magazines, and comics. It automatically renews at $11.99 per month unless you cancel.

You might also see an offer for two months for $0.99 total. That’s not free, but it’s worth comparing with the trial before you choose. The best tech deal this week The Apple iPhone 18 Pro is free right now with T-Mobile.

The Apple iPhone 18 Pro is free right now with T-Mobile.

And despite the name, you don’t need an iPhone to use it — Apple Music also works on Android and Windows.

Spotify Premium Individual — One month free for people who haven’t tried Premium before, then $12.99 per month. Includes ad-free music and offline downloads.

Sources indicate that deezer Family — One month free, then $19.99 per month. Cancel anytime.

According to recent reports, not all reading has to involve sitting down with a book. Audible’s 30-day free trial lets new customers choose one audiobook from its collection, including bestsellers and new releases, and listen to an included catalog of podcasts. After the trial, it automatically renews at $8.99 per month unless you cancel.

There’s also a separate promotion for three months at $0.99 per month, plus a $20 Audible bonus. I wouldn’t call that free, but paying $2.97 for three months might make more sense than taking one free month and then paying the regular rate.

In a recent development, hoopla — Free through participating public libraries. Check whether your library offers access before signing up; this is library borrowing, not a subscription trial that turns into a monthly bill.

According to recent reports, kobo Plus Listen — 14 days free, then $7.99 per month. The Read & Listen proposal includes both ebooks and audiobooks for $9.99 per month after the trial. You can use the Kobo Books app on your phone or tablet, so there’s no need to buy an e-reader.

According to recent reports, everand — 30 days free, with aims starting at $11.99 per month afterward. The trial includes one premium-title unlock, plus unlimited access to a separate catalog of more than 20,000 audiobooks, ebooks, and podcasts.

According to recent reports, all You Can Books — 30 days free, then $24.99 per month. The service advertises unlimited downloads from its catalog of audiobooks, ebooks, language courses, and other content, and claims downloaded files remain yours even after cancellation.

In a recent development, I’d use the free month to check whether the publications you actually want to read are included. A long list of magazines sounds nice, but it doesn’t mean much if you’re only opening one of them.

After the trial, the subscription costs $14.99 per month, so it's worth setting a reminder to cancel if you don't blueprint on keeping it.

Sources indicate that if you've been thinking about switching phone providers, Verizon is also offering a 30-day free trial, giving you a chance to test its network without switching providers. You can keep your existing phone number and continue using your current network while trying Verizon through an eSIM. There's no credit card required, no contract, and no need to remember to cancel, either. The trial automatically expires after 30 days, so you won't be charged if you decide not to switch.

In a recent development, T-Mobile — 30 days free for eligible non-T-Mobile customers with a compatible, unlocked device. Includes access to T-Mobile's network, satellite coverage, and member benefits, with no credit card, credit check, or commitment required.

Visible — 15 days free with unlimited data, talk, text, and hotspot access on Verizon's network. No credit card, contract, or automatic renewal required.

AT&T Wireless — 30 days free with unlimited talk and text, plus 100GB of data. Keep your current phone, number, and service while testing the network. Compatible iPhone or Android required.

And if you're planning to pick up a new Apple device during the Black Friday sales, you could get an even better deal, with three months free when you purchase an eligible device.

Glo — 7 days free, with access to more than 12,000 on-demand yoga, Pilates, meditation, and strength classes led by over 60 instructors.

Peloton App — Free trial for new members, with access to thousands of workout classes across more than 15 exercise types, including options that don't require equipment. Cancel anytime.

Ladder — 7 days free, with access to all training plans, personalized workout recommendations, introductory classes, and fitness communities. No payment information required to start the trial.

Nike Training Club — Completely free, with access to guided workouts, multi-week training programs, and fitness advice. No subscription or trial period required.

If you're looking for a way to unwind after a busy day, Calm is offering a seven-day free trial of its Premium membership. You'll get access to more than 50,000 minutes of content, including guided meditations, Sleep Stories, relaxing music, and nature sounds. After the trial, the subscription automatically renews at $79.99 per year, plus applicable taxes, so make sure you cancel before the seven days are up if you don't want to continue.

If you're a sports fan seeking a Black Friday streaming deal, Fox One is your best option this year.

Recent findings suggest that what exactly does a Fox One subscription get you? A whole lot of sports, including live Sunday afternoon NFL games, Big Ten college football matchups, college basketball, MLB, NASCAR, and the list goes on. Sure, a month of streaming isn't that long, but you'll get access to a surprising number of games. This week alone would grant you access to the Eagles vs. Cowboys Thanksgiving Day game, West Virginia vs. Utah on Black Friday, in-market college football on Saturday, and in-market Sunday afternoon NFL games.

In a recent development, when you're not watching live sports, Fox One also unlocks your local Fox station and Fox Entertainment on demand, including movies, TV shows (like MasterChef and The Simpsons), and a bunch more. For $4.99, it's certainly worth a shot. Just remember to cancel before the month is up if you want to avoid the full charge.
